@renamed_parameters(f="frequency")
def read_shortcircuit_results(
    net,
    *,
    t_k_s: Optional[float] = None,
    n_factor: float = 1.0,
    frequency: float = 50.0,
    buses: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Read a solved pandapower short-circuit case as IEC 60909 quantities.

    Converts ``net.res_bus_sc`` into a tidy, unit-explicit
    :class:`polars.DataFrame` in which the quantities missing from
    pandapower's single line-to-earth path (``kappa``, ``i_p``, ``I_th``)
    are filled in, and ``I_th`` is recomputed with a DC heat factor that is
    correct in the ``kappa -> 2`` limit. See the module docstring for the
    reasoning.

    The fault type, case and clearing time are taken from ``net._options``
    (written by ``calc_sc``) so that a solved net is self-describing; the
    ``t_k_s`` and ``n_factor`` arguments override them. The clearing time
    is adopted only when the ``calc_sc`` run genuinely carried one --
    pandapower stores its signature default ``tk_s=1.0`` even for a run
    that asked for no thermal current at all, and passing that placeholder
    off as a protection setting is unsafe; see :func:`_tk_s_from_options`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    net : pandapower.auxiliary.pandapowerNet
        A pandapower network on which ``pandapower.shortcircuit.calc_sc``
        has already been run.
    t_k_s : float, optional
        Short-circuit duration ``T_k`` in seconds. Defaults to the
        ``tk_s`` of the ``calc_sc`` run, but only if that run requested a
        thermal-equivalent current (``ith=True``) or passed a ``tk_s``
        other than pandapower's default of 1.0 s. Without it ``m`` and
        ``I_th`` cannot be computed and are reported as ``None``.
    n_factor : float, default 1.0
        IEC 60909-0 AC heat factor ``n``. ``1.0`` is the
        far-from-generator case. pandapower does not model ``n``, so this
        argument is the only source of a non-neutral value.
    frequency : float, default 50.0
        System frequency in Hz used in the ``m`` factor.
        The former keyword ``f`` is accepted as a deprecated alias.
    buses : sequence of int, optional
        Restrict the output to these pandapower bus indices. Defaults to
        every bus in ``res_bus_sc``.

    Returns
    -------
    polars.DataFrame
        One row per bus with the columns ``pp_bus_index``, ``bus_name``,
        ``vn_kv``, ``fault_type``, ``case``, ``i_k_a`` (in **amperes**,
        not kA), ``r1_ohm``, ``x1_ohm``, ``r0_ohm``, ``x0_ohm``,
        ``r_to_x``, ``kappa``, ``kappa_origin``, ``t_k_s``, ``n_factor``,
        ``m``, ``i_p_a`` and ``i_th_a``.

    Raises
    ------
    ImportError
        If pandapower is not installed.
    ValueError
        If ``net`` carries no short-circuit results, or if ``buses``
        references indices absent from them.

    Warns
    -----
    InputWarning
        ``SC_KAPPA_OUT_OF_RANGE`` (a bus whose ``ip``/``ikss`` imply a
        ``kappa`` outside ``(1, 2]``; the closed form is used) and
        ``SC_KAPPA_MISSING`` (buses for which no ``kappa`` can be derived).

    Notes
    -----
    ``kappa_origin`` documents where each peak factor came from:
    ``"pandapower"`` (recovered from ``ip_ka``, topology-aware),
    ``"iec_closed_form"`` (``1.02 + 0.98*exp(-3*R/X)``) or
    ``"unavailable"``. Keep it in reports — it is the difference between a
    reproducible study and a magic number.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import pandapower.shortcircuit as sc  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> sc.calc_sc(net, fault="1ph", case="max", tk_s=0.5)  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> gi.read_shortcircuit_results(net).select("bus_name", "i_k_a", "kappa")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    require_pandapower()

    res = getattr(net, "res_bus_sc", None)
    if res is None or len(res) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "The pandapower net carries no short-circuit results. Run "
            "pandapower.shortcircuit.calc_sc(net, fault='1ph', case='max', "
            "ip=True, ith=True, tk_s=...) before calling "
            "read_shortcircuit_results()."
        )

    options: Dict[str, Any] = dict(getattr(net, "_options", None) or {})
    fault_type = str(options.get("fault", "unknown"))
    case = str(options.get("case", "unknown"))
    if t_k_s is None:
        t_k_s = _tk_s_from_options(options)
    if t_k_s is not None:
        t_k_s = float(t_k_s)
        if t_k_s <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"t_k_s must be strictly positive, got {t_k_s!r}.")
    if not (0.0 < float(n_factor) <= 1.0):
        raise ValueError(f"n_factor must lie in (0, 1], got {n_factor!r}.")
    n_factor = float(n_factor)

    # ``fault="1ph"`` is the earth-fault case; anything reporting a
    # zero-sequence impedance is treated the same way.
    earth_fault = fault_type in _EARTH_FAULT_TYPES or "rk0_ohm" in res.columns

    index_to_name = bus_index_to_name(net)

    if buses is not None:
        wanted = [int(b) for b in buses]
        missing = [b for b in wanted if b not in res.index]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Bus indices {missing} have no short-circuit results. "
                f"Available: {sorted(int(i) for i in res.index)}."
            )
        selection = wanted
    else:
        selection = [int(i) for i in res.index]

    rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for idx in selection:
        row = res.loc[idx]
        bus_name = index_to_name.get(idx, f"bus_{idx}")

        ikss_ka = _finite(row.get("ikss_ka"))
        i_k_a = None if ikss_ka is None else ikss_ka * 1000.0
        r1 = _finite(row.get("rk_ohm"))
        x1 = _finite(row.get("xk_ohm"))
        r0 = _finite(row.get("rk0_ohm"))
        x0 = _finite(row.get("xk0_ohm"))

        r_to_x = _loop_r_to_x(r1, x1, r0, x0, earth_fault)
        kappa, kappa_origin = _kappa_for_row(
            i_k_a, _finite(row.get("ip_ka")), r_to_x, bus_name
        )

        m = None
        i_p_a = None
        i_th_a = None
        if kappa is not None:
            if i_k_a is not None:
                i_p_a = peak_short_circuit_current(i_k_a, kappa)
            if t_k_s is not None:
                m = iec60909_m(kappa, frequency, t_k_s)
                if i_k_a is not None:
                    i_th_a = thermal_equivalent_current(i_k_a, m, n_factor)

        rows.append(
            {
                "pp_bus_index": int(idx),
                "bus_name": bus_name,
                "vn_kv": _finite(net.bus.at[idx, "vn_kv"]) if idx in net.bus.index else None,
                "fault_type": fault_type,
                "case": case,
                "i_k_a": i_k_a,
                "r1_ohm": r1,
                "x1_ohm": x1,
                "r0_ohm": r0,
                "x0_ohm": x0,
                "r_to_x": r_to_x,
                "kappa": kappa,
                "kappa_origin": kappa_origin,
                "t_k_s": t_k_s,
                "n_factor": n_factor,
                "m": m,
                "i_p_a": i_p_a,
                "i_th_a": i_th_a,
            }
        )

    unavailable = [r["bus_name"] for r in rows if r["kappa_origin"] == "unavailable"]
    if unavailable:
        emit(
            InputWarning,
            f"No kappa could be derived for {len(unavailable)} bus(es) "
            f"({unavailable}): neither ip_ka nor a usable R/X is available. For "
            f"fault='1ph' make sure the zero-sequence data (x0x_max, r0x0_max, "
            f"vk0_percent, r0_ohm_per_km, ...) is complete.",
            code="SC_KAPPA_MISSING",
            elements=[("bus", name) for name in unavailable],
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    return pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=_SC_SCHEMA)

docs.title: Project files (JSON)
docs.text:
gi.save_network_to_json(network, path) writes one network to a project file, and gi.load_network_from_json(path) reads it back. The file is the network's own model_dump_json(indent=4) with two header keys in front:

{
    "schema_version": 1,
    "groundinsight_version": "2026.11.0",
    "name": "Umspannwerk Süd",
    "description": null,
    "frequencies": [50.0, 250.0],
    ...
}
  • UTF-8 on every platform. Names such as "Umspannwerk Süd Ω" are stored as UTF-8 regardless of the locale; up to 0.6.0 the locale decided, which on Windows (cp1252) meant a UnicodeEncodeError for Ω/ρ and mojibake for a file written on macOS. A UTF-8 byte-order mark is accepted on reading. A file that is not UTF-8 can only come from 0.6.0 or earlier on a non-UTF-8 system; it is read with the platform's preferred encoding, as 0.6.0 did, and an InputWarning with the code PROJECT_FILE_LEGACY_ENCODING says so. Saving it again writes UTF-8.
  • Atomic. The network is serialised completely, written to a temporary file in the target directory, flushed and fsync-ed, and only then moved over the target with os.replace. A failure at any point leaves an existing project file byte-identical. The replaced file keeps its permission bits, a read-only file is refused, and a symbolic link keeps pointing at the saved file.
  • Versioned. schema_version is the version of the file layout, groundinsight_version the release that wrote it (see the table below).
schema_version Written by Content (absent) 0.6.0 and earlier the model dump only — read unchanged 1 the first release after 0.6.0 and later the two header keys plus the model dump

A file with a newer schema_version than the running release supports is refused with a ValueError that names both versions, instead of being read with whatever the newer release added silently dropped. The version is incremented whenever a release writes something an earlier release would ignore or misread.

The header keys sit next to the model fields rather than in an envelope on purpose: Network ignores unknown keys, so gi.Network.model_validate_json(text) still reads a project file — and a 0.6.0 installation still opens a file written by a newer release of the same schema. load_network_from_json removes the two keys before validation and therefore does not depend on that. The names schema_version and groundinsight_version are reserved; Network never gets fields of that name.

docs.title: project_file
docs.text:
The JSON project file: one network per file, UTF-8, written atomically.

A project file is what :func:save_network_to_json writes and :func:load_network_from_json reads -- the network's own model_dump_json(indent=4) with two header keys in front::

{
    "schema_version": 1,
    "groundinsight_version": "2026.11.0",
    "name": "...",
    ...
}

Three properties are guaranteed, because a desktop application and a server open and save these files on every platform:

Encoding The file is UTF-8 on every platform. Without an explicit encoding the locale decides: on Windows (cp1252) a name containing Ω or ρ raises UnicodeEncodeError on save, and a file with "Süd" written on macOS comes back as mojibake. Reading accepts a UTF-8 byte-order mark, which Windows editors add when a file is edited by hand. A file that is not UTF-8 can only have been written by 0.6.0 or earlier with a non-UTF-8 locale; it is decoded with the platform's preferred encoding -- exactly what 0.6.0 did on that machine -- and an :class:~groundinsight.InputWarning with the code PROJECT_FILE_LEGACY_ENCODING says so. Saving it again writes UTF-8.

Atomicity The network is serialised completely before anything touches the disk, then written to a temporary file in the target directory, flushed and fsync-ed, and moved over the target with :func:os.replace. A failure at any point -- an exception in the serialiser, a full disk, a crash -- leaves an existing file byte-identical and removes the temporary file. The 0.6.0 writer truncated the target first, so the same failures left an empty or half-written project. The replaced file keeps the permission bits of the old one (a new file gets the usual 0o666 & ~umask), a read-only target is refused like open("w") refuses it, and a symbolic link is followed so the link keeps pointing at the saved file.

Schema version schema_version (an int) is the version of the file layout; groundinsight_version (a str) names the release that wrote it. A reader refuses a schema_version newer than :data:SCHEMA_VERSION with a :class:ValueError that names both numbers, instead of silently dropping whatever the newer release added. Files without the keys -- plain model_dump_json dumps, the format of groundinsight 0.6.0 and earlier -- load as a network without metadata.

Where the metadata lives, and why not in an envelope

The two keys sit next to the model fields rather than in an envelope such as {"format": ..., "network": {...}}. Network does not forbid extra keys (its model_config leaves extra at Pydantic's default "ignore"), so Network.model_validate_json -- the documented way to read a dump, used in the docs and by every script written against 0.6.0 -- still accepts a project file, and a 0.6.0 reader opens a new file too. An envelope would break both. The reader here does not rely on extra being "ignore": it removes the two keys before validation, so a later extra="forbid" on Network cannot lock out project files. The names are therefore reserved: Network must never get a field called schema_version or groundinsight_version.

When to increment :data:SCHEMA_VERSION

Whenever a release writes something an earlier release would ignore or misread -- a new field that changes a result, a changed meaning of an existing one, a different shape of a stored value. The older release then refuses the file instead of computing with a silently reduced model. A change that older releases read correctly (a new optional field they may safely ignore) does not need a new version.

The validation itself is the model's: after the metadata check the parsed object goes through Network.model_validate, the same validators and formula guard as every other way of building a network. (Validating the parsed dictionary gives the same model as Network.model_validate_json on the text -- the tests compare both on every value shape that serialises specially -- and is faster, because the file is parsed once.)

def load_network_from_json(path: _PathLike) -> Network:
    """
    Load a network from a JSON project file.

    Reads files of every release: files with the current or an older
    ``schema_version``, and files without one (written by 0.6.0 or earlier).

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : str or os.PathLike
        The project file.

    Returns
    -------
    Network
        The validated network, including any stored results.

    Raises
    ------
    OSError
        If the file cannot be read.
    ValueError
        If the file is not valid JSON, is not a JSON object, is neither UTF-8
        nor in the platform's preferred encoding, carries an invalid or a
        newer ``schema_version`` than :data:`SCHEMA_VERSION`, or does not
        describe a valid network (``pydantic.ValidationError`` is a
        ``ValueError``).

    Warns
    -----
    InputWarning
        Code ``PROJECT_FILE_LEGACY_ENCODING``: the file is not UTF-8 and was
        decoded with the platform's preferred encoding, as 0.6.0 wrote it on
        that machine.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> net = gi.load_network_from_json("sued.json")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    source = os.fspath(path)
    with open(source, "rb") as handle:
        raw = handle.read()
    text, legacy_encoding = _decode(raw, source)
    try:
        payload = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"'{source}' is not a valid JSON file: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ValueError(
            f"'{source}' does not contain a groundinsight network: the "
            f"top-level JSON value is a {type(payload).__name__}, not an object."
        )
    schema_version, written_by = _pop_metadata(payload, source)
    if legacy_encoding is not None and schema_version is not None:
        # Every release that writes a schema version writes UTF-8, so a file
        # with one that is not UTF-8 has been re-encoded or damaged since.
        raise ValueError(
            f"'{source}' carries schema_version {schema_version} but is not "
            "valid UTF-8; project files with a schema version are always "
            "written as UTF-8. Re-encode the file as UTF-8."
        )
    network = Network.model_validate(payload)
    if legacy_encoding is not None:
        emit(
            InputWarning,
            f"'{source}' is not UTF-8 and was decoded with the platform's "
            f"preferred encoding '{legacy_encoding}', the way groundinsight "
            "0.6.0 and earlier wrote project files. Names may be garbled if "
            "the file was written on a computer with a different locale. "
            "Saving the network again writes UTF-8.",
            code="PROJECT_FILE_LEGACY_ENCODING",
            elements=[("network", network.name)],
        )
    logger.debug(
        "Loaded network '%s' from '%s' (schema version %s, written by "
        "groundinsight %s).",
        network.name,
        source,
        schema_version if schema_version is not None else "none",
        written_by if written_by is not None else "0.6.0 or earlier",
    )
    return network

def save_network_to_json(network: Network, path: _PathLike) -> None:
    """
    Save a network to a JSON project file, atomically and as UTF-8.

    The file is the network's ``model_dump_json(indent=4)`` preceded by the
    header keys ``schema_version`` (:data:`SCHEMA_VERSION`) and
    ``groundinsight_version``. Stored results are included.

    Parameters
    ----------
    network : Network
        The network to save.
    path : str or os.PathLike
        Target file. An existing file is replaced as a whole or not at all;
        if ``path`` is a symbolic link, the file it points to is replaced.

    Raises
    ------
    OSError
        If the file cannot be written (directory missing, disk full,
        read-only target, ...). An existing file is then left byte-identical
        and no temporary file remains.
    Exception
        Whatever the serialiser raises; the disk is not touched in that case.

    Notes
    -----
    The new content is written to a temporary file next to the target,
    flushed and ``fsync``-ed, and then moved over the target with
    :func:`os.replace`, which is atomic on POSIX and Windows. The directory
    entry is ``fsync``-ed afterwards where the platform supports it.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> net = gi.create_network(name="Süd", frequencies=[50.0])
    >>> gi.save_network_to_json(net, "sued.json")  # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> gi.load_network_from_json("sued.json").name  # doctest: +SKIP
    'Süd'
    """
    # Serialise first: a failure here must not have touched the disk.
    payload = _project_file_text(network).encode("utf-8")
    target = _resolve_target(os.fspath(path))
    _atomic_write(target, payload)
    logger.debug(
        "Saved network '%s' to '%s' (schema version %d).",
        network.name,
        target,
        SCHEMA_VERSION,
    )

docs.title: Network operations
docs.text: High-level factory functions to build a Network and run fault calculations. These are the functions re-exported on the top-level package as groundinsight.create_network, groundinsight.run_fault, etc.

docs.title: Physical / modelling context
docs.text:
A Network is a graph: each Bus represents a grounding node with an own electrode impedance \(Z_B(f, \rho)\) (not the earthing impedance \(Z_E\) of EN 50522, which run_fault computes at the fault bus), every Branch a metallic return path with self-impedance \(Z_\text{branch}(f, l)\) and an optional mutual coupling that appears as a Norton injection along the source-to-fault path. Building the network and triggering a fault therefore requires four ingredients:

  1. Types — BusType, BranchType carrying SymPy formula strings in the free symbols rho, f and (for branches) l.
  2. Instances — Bus, Branch with concrete values for specific_earth_resistance, length, parallel_coefficient.
  3. Excitation — at least one Source (current or voltage) and one Fault declaring which bus is the ground-fault location and which fault scaling per frequency applies.
  4. Frequency list — the harmonics or per-fault spectrum at which the formula-based impedances are evaluated.

run_fault then assembles the nodal admittance matrix, runs the sparse LU solve per frequency, and stores the result on the Network (net.results).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import groundinsight as gi

# 1. Frequency list and types
net = gi.create_network(name="demo", frequencies=[50.0, 250.0])
bus_type = gi.BusType(
    name="GroundRod",
    system_type="Substation",
    voltage_level=20.0,
    impedance_formula="rho/(2*3.14159*1.5)*(1 + j*0.01*f)",
)
branch_type = gi.BranchType(
    name="ShieldCable",
    grounding_conductor=True,
    self_impedance_formula="(0.2 + j*0.4*f/50)*l",
    mutual_impedance_formula="(0.0 + j*0.4*f/50)*l",
)

# 2. Instances
gi.create_bus(name="bus_substation", type=bus_type,
              specific_earth_resistance=100.0, network=net)
gi.create_bus(name="bus_fault", type=bus_type,
              specific_earth_resistance=100.0, network=net)
gi.create_branch(name="line_1", type=branch_type,
                 from_bus="bus_substation", to_bus="bus_fault",
                 length=2.0, network=net)

# 3. Source and fault
gi.create_source(name="src1", bus="bus_substation",
                 values={50.0: 1.0, 250.0: 0.05}, network=net)
gi.create_fault(name="f1", bus="bus_fault",
                scalings={50.0: 1.0, 250.0: 0.05}, network=net)

# 4. Run
gi.run_fault(network=net, fault="f1")
print(net.res_buses(fault="f1"))

The same workflow scales to multi-source ring or mesh topologies. The default phase_current_mode="auto" splits the phase current of a meshed network by solving the phase-conductor network itself; give the branch types a phase_impedance_formula, otherwise the split uses proxy impedances and the result says so (PHASE_PROXY).

docs.title: A network without excitation is rejected
docs.text:
Step 3 is not optional. A network without a source or without a fault has nothing that drives a current, and the calculation used to run to completion anyway and report 0 V at every bus. That is a plausible-looking answer, and the most common way to arrive at it is a forgotten gi.create_source(...), not a network that is genuinely unexcited. run_fault (and the path enumeration of Pathfinder) now raises a ValueError naming the missing side.

A fault that no source reaches over active elements is a different matter and stays permitted: that is exactly what an outage scenario islanding the fault bus produces, and 0 V is then the correct answer. gi.check_network reports it (FAULT_NOT_REACHED).

docs.title: create_network_assistant and the n−1 rule
docs.text:
A line of n buses has n − 1 branches, so branch_length needs n − 1 entries:

net = gi.create_network_assistant(
    name="Line30", frequencies=[50.0, 250.0], number_buses=30,
    bus_type=bus_type, branch_type=branch_type,
    branch_length=[1.0] * 29,          # 29, not 30
    specific_earth_resistance=100.0,
)

Passing n lengths used to drop the last one silently — the two tests in this repository that did so had been asserting against a shorter line than they thought for as long as they existed — and passing too few raised a bare IndexError from inside the loop. Both now raise a ValueError that states the two counts.

docs.title: network_operations
docs.text:
Network Operations Module.

This module provides functions for managing the electrical network, including creating networks, buses, branches, faults, and sources. It also includes functions to build the electrical network, define paths, and run fault calculations. These operations utilize the core models defined in groundinsight.models.core_models and interact with the Network instance to perform necessary calculations and updates.

def build_electrical_network(network: Network, auto_phase_currents: bool = False):
    """
    Build the electrical network and attach it to the :class:`Network` object.

    Initialises an :class:`ElectricalNetwork` helper based on the physical
    network's configuration and assigns it to the
    ``electrical_network`` attribute of the provided :class:`Network`
    instance. This step is invoked automatically by :func:`run_fault`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    network : Network
        The network instance for which the electrical network is to be
        built.
    auto_phase_currents : bool, optional
        If ``True``, the phase current through each branch is determined
        by solving a reduced phase-conductor network (topology-based
        split over parallel paths). If ``False``, the phase current is
        derived from the enumerated source-to-fault paths using each
        branch's ``parallel_coefficient``. Defaults to ``False`` here;
        :func:`run_fault` passes ``True`` unless asked otherwise.

    Raises
    ------
    ImportError
        If the :class:`ElectricalNetwork` class cannot be imported.
    ValueError
        If a source that reaches the active fault has a value at none of the
        network frequencies. The checks of the input that
        :func:`run_fault` makes run here, while the vectors are assembled.

    Warns
    -----
    InputWarning
        ``SOURCE_FREQUENCY_GAP`` for a source that misses some network
        frequencies, ``SCALINGS_INCOMPLETE`` for an incomplete
        ``Fault.scalings``.
    ModelAssumptionWarning
        ``THEVENIN_COUPLING`` for a Thevenin source that drives coupled
        branches.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
    >>> net = build_minimal()
    >>> net.set_active_fault("fault")
    >>> gi.build_electrical_network(net)
    >>> net.electrical_network.bus_indices
    {'bus1': 0, 'bus2': 1, 'bus3': 2}
    """
    from groundinsight.electrical_network import ElectricalNetwork

    network.electrical_network = ElectricalNetwork(
        network, auto_phase_currents=auto_phase_currents, input_checks=True
    )

def create_branch(
    name: str,
    type: BranchType,
    from_bus: str,
    to_bus: str,
    length: float,
    specific_earth_resistance: Optional[float] = 100,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    network: Optional[Network] = None,
    parallel_coefficient: Optional[float] = 1.0,
) -> Branch:
    """
    Create a new :class:`Branch` instance and optionally add it to a network.

    If a :class:`Network` instance is provided, the branch is added to the
    network, which also triggers the self- and mutual-impedance
    calculations against the network's frequency list.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The name of the branch.
    type : BranchType
        The type of the branch.
    from_bus : str
        The name of the originating bus.
    to_bus : str
        The name of the terminating bus.
    length : float
        The length of the branch in km; finite and strictly positive.
    specific_earth_resistance : float, optional
        The specific earth resistance for the branch (Ohm * m). Defaults
        to ``100``.
    description : str, optional
        A brief description of the branch. Defaults to ``None``.
    network : Network, optional
        The network to which the branch should be added. Defaults to
        ``None``.
    parallel_coefficient : float, optional
        Per-branch share of the source-to-fault phase current; used by
        the path-based mutual-coupling injection. Defaults to ``1.0``.
        **Only read in the legacy phase-current mode**
        ``run_fault(..., phase_current_mode="paths")``. The default mode
        ``"auto"`` solves a reduced phase-conductor network from
        ``BranchType.phase_impedance_formula``, where the split follows from
        the phase impedances and this value is ignored.

    Returns
    -------
    Branch
        A newly created :class:`Branch` instance.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the specified ``from_bus`` or ``to_bus`` does not exist in the
        provided network, if ``length`` is not a finite positive number of
        km, or if the impedances cannot be derived from ``type``. The
        network is unchanged in every case.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> branch_type = gi.BranchType(
    ...     name="StandardBranch", grounding_conductor=True,
    ...     self_impedance_formula="(1 + j * f / 50)*l",
    ...     mutual_impedance_formula="(0.5 + j * f / 100)*l",
    ... )
    >>> branch = gi.create_branch(
    ...     name="Branch1", type=branch_type,
    ...     from_bus="Bus1", to_bus="Bus2", length=1.0,
    ... )
    >>> branch.name
    'Branch1'
    """
    # Validate buses if network is provided
    if network:
        if from_bus not in network.buses:
            raise ValueError(
                f"from_bus '{from_bus}' is not in the network '{network.name}'"
            )
        if to_bus not in network.buses:
            raise ValueError(
                f"to_bus '{to_bus}' is not in the network '{network.name}'"
            )

    branch = Branch(
        name=name,
        type=type,
        length=length,
        from_bus=from_bus,
        to_bus=to_bus,
        specific_earth_resistance=specific_earth_resistance,
        self_impedance={},  # Will be calculated
        mutual_impedance={},  # Will be calculated
        description=description,
        parallel_coefficient=parallel_coefficient,
    )
    if network:
        network.add_branch(branch)
        # Impedance calculations are triggered within network.add_branch()
    return branch

    network's frequency list.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str

    specific_earth_resistance : float, optional

def create_fault(
    name: str,
    bus: str,
    scalings: Optional[Dict] = None,
    active: bool = False,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    network: Optional[Network] = None,
    t_k_s: Optional[float] = None,
    n_factor: float = 1.0,
) -> Fault:
    """
    Create a new :class:`Fault` instance and optionally add it to a network.

    If a :class:`Network` instance is provided, the fault is added to the
    network. If ``active=True``, the fault becomes the currently active
    fault in the network.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The name of the fault.
    bus : str
        The name of the bus where the fault occurs.
    scalings : dict of float to float, optional
        Factor applied to the source currents, per frequency. ``None`` (the
        default) or ``{}`` means 1.0 at every frequency. A frequency missing
        from a non-empty mapping is scaled with 1.0 as well -- full
        contribution, not zero -- and ``run_fault`` announces the incomplete
        mapping once per run (``InputWarning`` ``SCALINGS_INCOMPLETE``). Give
        ``0.0`` to exclude a frequency from this fault.
    active : bool, optional
        Whether to activate the fault immediately upon creation. Defaults
        to ``False``.
    description : str, optional
        A brief description of the fault. Defaults to ``None``.
    network : Network, optional
        The network to which the fault should be added. Defaults to
        ``None``.
    t_k_s : float, optional
        IEC 60909-0 short-circuit duration ``T_k`` in seconds. When set,
        :func:`groundinsight.check_conductor_limits` can derive the
        thermal rating without an explicit ``t_k`` argument.
    n_factor : float, default 1.0
        IEC 60909-0 AC heat factor ``n``. Keep the default ``1.0`` for
        far-from-generator faults, which is the normal case in grounding
        studies.

    Returns
    -------
    Fault
        A newly created :class:`Fault` instance.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the specified bus does not exist in the provided network, if
        ``t_k_s`` is not a positive duration, if ``n_factor`` lies
        outside ``(0, 1]``, or if ``active=True`` is passed without a
        network. The network is unchanged in every case.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> bus_type = gi.BusType(
    ...     name="StandardBus", system_type="Grounded", voltage_level=110,
    ...     impedance_formula="1 + j * f / 50",
    ... )
    >>> network = gi.create_network(name="TestNetwork", frequencies=[50, 60])
    >>> _ = gi.create_bus(name="Bus1", type=bus_type, network=network)
    >>> fault = gi.create_fault(
    ...     name="Fault1", bus="Bus1",
    ...     scalings={50: 1.0, 60: 0.8},
    ...     active=True, network=network,
    ... )
    >>> fault.name
    'Fault1'
    """
    if active and network is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"create_fault(name='{name}', active=True) needs a network: a "
            "fault can only be the active one *in* a network. Pass "
            "network=..., or leave active=False and call "
            "network.set_active_fault(...) once the fault has been added."
        )
    if network and bus not in network.buses:
        raise ValueError(f"bus '{bus}' is not in the network '{network.name}'")

    fault = Fault(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        bus=bus,
        scalings=scalings,
        t_k_s=t_k_s,
        n_factor=n_factor,
    )

    if network:
        network.add_fault(fault)

    if active:
        network.set_active_fault(name)

    return fault

def create_network_assistant(
    name: str,
    frequencies: List,
    number_buses: int,
    bus_type: BusType,
    branch_type: BranchType,
    branch_length: List,
    specific_earth_resistance: float,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Network:
    """
    Create a linear network with a uniform bus and branch type.

    Initialises a :class:`Network` instance and populates it with
    ``number_buses`` buses and ``number_buses - 1`` branches connected
    sequentially to form a line topology. Impedance calculations are
    triggered upon adding buses and branches to the network.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The name of the network.
    frequencies : list of float
        Frequencies (in Hz) at which network calculations are performed.
    number_buses : int
        The total number of buses to create.
    bus_type : BusType
        The type to assign to each bus.
    branch_type : BranchType
        The type to assign to each branch.
    branch_length : list of float
        Lengths of each branch connecting the buses. Must have
        ``number_buses - 1`` elements.
    specific_earth_resistance : float
        The specific earth resistance for all buses and branches
        (Ohm * m).
    description : str, optional
        A brief description of the network. Defaults to ``None``.

    Returns
    -------
    Network
        A fully initialised :class:`Network` instance with the specified
        configuration.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``number_buses`` is not an integer ``>= 1``, or if the length
        of ``branch_length`` does not match ``number_buses - 1``.

    Notes
    -----
    A line of ``n`` buses has ``n - 1`` branches, so ``branch_length``
    has one entry *fewer* than ``number_buses``. Passing ``n`` lengths --
    ``[1.0] * 30`` for ``number_buses=30``, read as "a 30 km line" -- is
    refused rather than truncated: dropping the surplus entry would return a
    network one span shorter than the one asked for, with no warning
    anywhere. Too few entries are refused the same way instead of failing
    with a bare ``IndexError`` from inside the loop.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> station = gi.BusType(name="station", system_type="Substation",
    ...                      voltage_level=20.0, impedance_formula="rho * 0.01")
    >>> cable = gi.BranchType(name="cable", grounding_conductor=True,
    ...                       self_impedance_formula="(0.25 + j * f * 0.012) * l",
    ...                       mutual_impedance_formula="j * f * 0.012 * l")
    >>> net = gi.create_network_assistant(
    ...     name="Linear5", frequencies=[50.0], number_buses=5, bus_type=station,
    ...     branch_type=cable, branch_length=[1.0] * 4, specific_earth_resistance=100.0)
    >>> list(net.buses), list(net.branches)
    (['bus1', 'bus2', 'bus3', 'bus4', 'bus5'], ['branch1', 'branch2', 'branch3', 'branch4'])
    """
    if isinstance(number_buses, bool) or not isinstance(number_buses, int):
        raise ValueError(
            f"number_buses must be an int >= 1, got "
            f"{number_buses!r} ({type(number_buses).__name__})."
        )
    if number_buses < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"number_buses must be >= 1, got {number_buses}.")

    try:
        n_lengths = len(branch_length)
    except TypeError:
        raise ValueError(
            f"branch_length must be a sequence of {number_buses - 1} lengths "
            f"(one per branch), got {branch_length!r} "
            f"({type(branch_length).__name__})."
        ) from None
    if n_lengths != number_buses - 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"branch_length has {n_lengths} entries but a line of "
            f"{number_buses} buses has {number_buses - 1} branches. "
            "A line of n buses needs n-1 lengths."
        )

    net = create_network(name, frequencies, description)

    for i in range(number_buses):
        # create a bus with the name "bus"+i+1
        bus_name = f"bus{i+1}"
        create_bus(bus_name, bus_type, specific_earth_resistance, network=net)
        if i > 0:
            # create a branch with the name "branch"+i which connectes the buses from idx i-1 and i
            branch_name = f"branch{i}"
            create_branch(
                branch_name,
                branch_type,
                f"bus{i}",
                bus_name,
                branch_length[i - 1],
                specific_earth_resistance,
                network=net,
            )

    return net

Create all paths between the sources and the faults of the network.

Identifies and maps each source to the ordered branch list of every simple path to each fault. The identified paths are added to the network's paths collection.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the network defines no sources or no faults. Path enumeration runs over sources x faults, so an empty side yields no paths at all; every downstream step then succeeds on an unexcited system and reports 0 V at every bus. That is a plausible-looking result, not an error message, so it is rejected here instead.

Notes

The check is on all faults, not on active_fault: :meth:~groundinsight.models.core_models.Network.define_paths enumerates every (source, fault) pair, and run_fault sets the active fault before it calls this function.

Finding no path between an existing source and an existing fault is a different matter and stays permitted -- that is exactly what an outage scenario which islands the fault bus produces, and the all-zero result is then the correct answer.

Examples:

Paths are what phase_current_mode="paths" reads:

>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
>>> net = build_minimal()
>>> gi.create_paths(net)
>>> [path.name for path in net.paths.values()]

def create_source(
    name: str,
    bus: str,
    values: Dict,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    network: Optional[Network] = None,
    i_k_a: Optional[float] = None,
    r_to_x: Optional[float] = None,
    kappa: Optional[float] = None,
) -> Source:
    """
    Create a new current :class:`Source` and optionally add it to a network.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The name of the source.
    bus : str
        The name of the bus where the source is located.
    values : dict of float to ComplexNumber or complex or float
        Frequency-resolved injected current. Real numbers are auto-promoted
        to :class:`ComplexNumber`.
    description : str, optional
        A brief description of the source. Defaults to ``None``.
    network : Network, optional
        The network to which the source should be added. Defaults to
        ``None``.
    i_k_a : float, optional
        Initial symmetrical short-circuit current ``I_k''`` in amperes
        contributed by this source. Metadata for the IEC 60909
        characteristics; the solve keeps using ``values``.
    r_to_x : float, optional
        ``R/X`` ratio of the short-circuit loop, used to derive ``kappa``
        when the latter is not given.
    kappa : float, optional
        IEC 60909-0 peak factor. Takes precedence over ``r_to_x``.

    Returns
    -------
    Source
        A newly created :class:`Source` instance with
        ``source_type='current'``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the specified bus does not exist in the provided network, or if
        any of the IEC 60909 quantities is outside its physical range.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> bus_type = gi.BusType(
    ...     name="StandardBus", system_type="Grounded", voltage_level=110,
    ...     impedance_formula="1 + j * f / 50",
    ... )
    >>> network = gi.create_network(name="TestNetwork", frequencies=[50, 60])
    >>> _ = gi.create_bus(name="Bus1", type=bus_type, network=network)
    >>> source = gi.create_source(
    ...     name="Source1", bus="Bus1",
    ...     values={50: 10 + 5j, 60: 15 + 7j},
    ...     network=network,
    ... )
    >>> source.name
    'Source1'
    """
    if network and bus not in network.buses:
        raise ValueError(f"bus '{bus}' is not in the network '{network.name}'")

    source = Source(
        name=name,
        description=description,
        bus=bus,
        values=values,
        i_k_a=i_k_a,
        r_to_x=r_to_x,
        kappa=kappa,
    )
    if network:
        network.add_source(source)
    return source

run_fault(
    network: Network,
    fault: str,
    auto_parallel_coefficients: Optional[bool] = None,
    *,
    phase_current_mode: str = "auto",
)

Execute the fault calculation pipeline for a single fault.

Sets the named fault as the active fault, builds the electrical network, solves the per-frequency nodal system, computes branch currents, reduction factors and grounding impedance. The results are stored on network.results[fault]. :func:groundinsight.solve runs the same pipeline without writing anything into network.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default network Network

The network instance on which the fault calculations are to be performed.

required fault str

The name of the fault to activate and run calculations for. The former keyword fault_name is accepted as a deprecated alias.

required auto_parallel_coefficients bool

Deprecated alias for phase_current_mode. True maps to "auto", False to "paths". When given it wins over phase_current_mode so existing call sites keep their exact behaviour. Defaults to None (not given).

None phase_current_mode (auto, paths)

How the phase current per branch is determined.

"auto" (default) solves a reduced phase-conductor network per source with the fault bus as reference and reads the branch currents off that solution. This is the only mode that splits the source current correctly over rings, meshes and parallel branches, and it ignores Branch.parallel_coefficient.

"paths": every branch on any enumerated source-to-fault path receives the full source current scaled by its parallel_coefficient. In a meshed network that multiplies the current instead of splitting it: in a symmetric ring of two routes, at the default coefficient of 1.0, the coupled injections add up to (1 - 2k) I instead of (1 - k) I (k = Z_m / Z_s). That collapses the EPR to 0 for k = 0.5 and, where |1 - 2k| = 1, reports it as if the shields did not couple at all. Kept for reproducing studies made with this scheme and for networks where the split is known from measurement and set by hand.

"auto"

Returns:

Type Description Result

The result of the run -- the same object that is stored as network.results[fault]. Its diagnostics list holds every package warning raised during the run, with code and element references (see :mod:groundinsight.diagnostics).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the specified fault does not exist in the network, if the network defines no sources or no faults at all, or if phase_current_mode is not one of the two accepted values.

RuntimeError

If there is an error during the network calculations.

Warns:

Type Description ModelAssumptionWarning

Among others (every package warning of the run is collected into Result.diagnostics): PARALLEL_COEFFICIENT_DEFAULT when phase_current_mode="paths" meets a source that reaches the fault over several paths with default parallel coefficients, and EARTH_GROUP_SPREAD when the electrode currents are spread in angle so that I_E and value_current describe the dominant direction only.

Notes

"auto" does not enumerate the source-to-fault paths. It only needs to know which sources reach the fault, which :meth:~groundinsight.models.core_models.Network.sources_reaching answers with a breadth-first search over the active sub-graph. The enumeration is exponential in the number of independent loops -- a 6x6 grid has 1 262 816 simple paths, about a minute of enumeration per run_fault while the solver itself needs milliseconds -- so it runs only in "paths" mode or when the user asks for it with :func:create_paths. network.paths is therefore normally empty after a default run_fault; a path set that no longer matches the active topology is dropped so no later reader picks it up.

Examples:

>>> import polars as pl
>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
>>> net = build_minimal()
>>> result = gi.run_fault(net, "fault")
>>> result is net.results["fault"]
True
>>> epr = net.res_buses("fault").filter(pl.col("is_rms"))
>>> [(row["bus_name"], round(row["EPR_V"], 2)) for row in epr.iter_rows(named=True)]
[('bus1', 18.03), ('bus2', 0.0), ('bus3', 18.03)]

def run_fault(
    network: Network,
    fault: str,
    auto_parallel_coefficients: Optional[bool] = None,
    *,
    phase_current_mode: str = "auto",
):
    """
    Execute the fault calculation pipeline for a single fault.

    Sets the named fault as the active fault, builds the electrical
    network, solves the per-frequency nodal system, computes branch
    currents, reduction factors and grounding impedance. The results are
    stored on ``network.results[fault]``. :func:`groundinsight.solve` runs the
    same pipeline without writing anything into ``network``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    network : Network
        The network instance on which the fault calculations are to be
        performed.
    fault : str
        The name of the fault to activate and run calculations for. The
        former keyword ``fault_name`` is accepted as a deprecated alias.
    auto_parallel_coefficients : bool, optional
        Deprecated alias for ``phase_current_mode``. ``True`` maps to
        ``"auto"``, ``False`` to ``"paths"``. When given it wins over
        ``phase_current_mode`` so existing call sites keep their exact
        behaviour. Defaults to ``None`` (not given).
    phase_current_mode : {"auto", "paths"}, optional
        How the phase current per branch is determined.

        ``"auto"`` (default) solves a reduced phase-conductor network per
        source with the fault bus as reference and reads the branch
        currents off that solution. This is the only mode that splits the
        source current correctly over rings, meshes and parallel
        branches, and it ignores ``Branch.parallel_coefficient``.

        ``"paths"``: every branch on any enumerated source-to-fault path
        receives the *full* source current scaled by its
        ``parallel_coefficient``. In a meshed network that multiplies the
        current instead of splitting it: in a symmetric ring of two routes,
        at the default coefficient of 1.0, the coupled injections add up to
        ``(1 - 2k) I`` instead of ``(1 - k) I`` (``k = Z_m / Z_s``). That
        collapses the EPR to 0 for ``k = 0.5`` and, where ``|1 - 2k| = 1``,
        reports it as if the shields did not couple at all. Kept for
        reproducing studies made with this scheme and for networks where the
        split is known from measurement and set by hand.

    Returns
    -------
    Result
        The result of the run -- the same object that is stored as
        ``network.results[fault]``. Its ``diagnostics`` list holds every
        package warning raised during the run, with code and element
        references (see :mod:`groundinsight.diagnostics`).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the specified fault does not exist in the network, if the
        network defines no sources or no faults at all, or if
        ``phase_current_mode`` is not one of the two accepted values.
    RuntimeError
        If there is an error during the network calculations.

    Warns
    -----
    ModelAssumptionWarning
        Among others (every package warning of the run is collected into
        ``Result.diagnostics``): ``PARALLEL_COEFFICIENT_DEFAULT`` when
        ``phase_current_mode="paths"`` meets a source that reaches the fault
        over several paths with default parallel coefficients, and
        ``EARTH_GROUP_SPREAD`` when the electrode currents are spread in angle
        so that ``I_E`` and ``value_current`` describe the dominant direction
        only.

    Notes
    -----
    ``"auto"`` does **not** enumerate the source-to-fault paths. It only
    needs to know which sources reach the fault, which
    :meth:`~groundinsight.models.core_models.Network.sources_reaching`
    answers with a breadth-first search over the active sub-graph. The
    enumeration is exponential in the number of independent loops -- a
    6x6 grid has 1 262 816 simple paths, about a minute of enumeration per
    ``run_fault`` while the solver itself needs milliseconds -- so it runs
    only in ``"paths"`` mode or when the user asks for it with
    :func:`create_paths`. ``network.paths`` is therefore normally empty
    after a default ``run_fault``; a path set that no longer matches the
    active topology is dropped so no later reader picks it up.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import polars as pl
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
    >>> net = build_minimal()
    >>> result = gi.run_fault(net, "fault")
    >>> result is net.results["fault"]
    True
    >>> epr = net.res_buses("fault").filter(pl.col("is_rms"))
    >>> [(row["bus_name"], round(row["EPR_V"], 2)) for row in epr.iter_rows(named=True)]
    [('bus1', 18.03), ('bus2', 0.0), ('bus3', 18.03)]
    """
    auto_phase_currents = _resolve_phase_current_mode(
        phase_current_mode, auto_parallel_coefficients
    )

    # Set the active fault
    network.set_active_fault(fault)

    # (Re)build paths when they are missing or the active topology changed
    # since they were last built (e.g. a manual Bus.active / Branch.active
    # flip or an in-place rewiring). Without this check run_fault would
    # silently reuse stale paths while the Y-matrix is rebuilt from the
    # current active flags, yielding a wrong EPR.
    #
    # Only the legacy ``phase_current_mode="paths"`` actually needs the
    # enumerated paths -- there they carry the phase current per branch.
    # ``"auto"`` (the default) solves a reduced phase-conductor network and
    # only needs to know *which* sources reach the fault, which
    # ``Network.sources_reaching`` answers with a breadth-first search. The
    # enumeration is exponential in the number of loops (1.26 million paths
    # and roughly a minute on a 6x6 grid, against milliseconds in the
    # solver), so it is not triggered in the default mode. Stale
    # paths are still dropped so that no later reader -- persistence, the
    # transient state-space solver, the short-circuit aggregation -- picks
    # up a path set that no longer matches the topology. Users who want the
    # paths as data keep asking for them with ``gi.create_paths(network)``.
    _assert_network_is_excited(network)
    # Every package warning raised from here on belongs to this run. The
    # sink is per thread/task (see groundinsight.diagnostics), so concurrent
    # runs keep their messages apart, and it records warnings the caller has
    # filtered out as well -- the result carries them either way.
    with collecting() as sink:
        if not auto_phase_currents:
            if network.needs_path_rebuild():
                network.invalidate_paths()
                create_paths(network)
        elif network.paths and network.needs_path_rebuild():
            network.invalidate_paths()

        # Warn only in the legacy mode, and only when the network around this
        # fault actually has parallel routes -- see _warning_parallel_coeffcient.
        if not auto_phase_currents:
            _warning_parallel_coeffcient(network, auto_phase_currents)

        # Build the electrical network from the physical network.
        # auto_phase_currents switches the phase-current determination from
        # the path-based scheme (parallel_coefficient per branch) to the
        # phase-network solve.
        build_electrical_network(network, auto_phase_currents=auto_phase_currents)

        # Solve the network
        network.electrical_network.solve_network()

        # Compute branch currents
        network.electrical_network.compute_branch_currents()

        # Compute reduction factors
        network.electrical_network.compute_reduction_factors()

        # Compute grounding impedance
        network.electrical_network.compute_grounding_impedance()

    # Results are stored in net.results within the ElectricalNetwork methods;
    # the diagnostics of the run are attached to that same object.
    result = network.results[fault]
    result.diagnostics = unique(sink)
    # Stamp the inputs the result was computed from; Network.stale_results
    # compares the stamp with the network's inputs at any later time (GUI3).
    result.input_digest = network.input_digest(fault)
    return result

docs.title: Outage and what-if studies
docs.text: The groundinsight.simulation.outage module turns the new active flag on Bus and Branch into a first-class what-if API. Multiple topology scenarios (e.g. "cable A out", "substation isolator open", "shield broken") can be evaluated against one base case in a single call, with comparison DataFrames produced automatically.

docs.title: Physical / modelling context
docs.text:
The nodal-admittance solver assembles \(Y(f)\,\underline{u}(f) = \underline{i}(f)\) over active elements only. An inactive Bus is removed from the system entirely (its row and column drop from \(Y\)); an inactive Branch contributes no self-admittance, no mutual-coupling Norton injection, and reports a zero current in the result — the open-circuit limit. The search for the sources that reach the fault skips inactive elements as well (and so does the path enumeration of the legacy phase_current_mode="paths"), which keeps the phase currents and their Norton injections consistent.

That makes maintenance scenarios, planned outages, broken shields, and N-1 contingencies expressible as scenarios without rebuilding the network. The outage_context context manager flips the listed elements to active=False for the duration of a with block and restores the previous state — including the cached path list — afterwards. run_outage_study orchestrates a base run plus one fault calculation per scenario and returns long-format Polars DataFrames with absolute and relative deltas against a reference scenario (default: the base case).

A scenario whose solve fails aborts the study by default (on_error="raise"). Pass on_error="record" to note it in OutageStudyResult.failures and carry on with the next scenario instead — the interesting scenarios of an outage study are exactly the ones that disconnect something, and "this outage is not survivable" is an answer rather than a reason to discard the other twenty. The base case is never covered by "record": without it every comparison in the result would be against nothing.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# fragment: assumes a network `net` with the branch "cable_1", the bus "bus_x" and the fault "fault1"
import groundinsight as gi

# Assume a pre-built network `net` with sources, buses, branches and
# at least one fault, e.g. from the quickstart or from
# gi.from_pandapower(...).

scenario_cable_out = gi.Outage(
    name="cable_1_oos",
    description="MS-cable cable_1 out of service",
    disabled_buses=[],
    disabled_branches=["cable_1"],
)

scenario_bus_islanded = gi.Outage(
    name="bus_x_islanded",
    description="Bus bus_x removed from the network",
    disabled_buses=["bus_x"],
    disabled_branches=[],
)

study = gi.run_outage_study(
    network=net,
    fault="fault1",
    scenarios=[scenario_cable_out, scenario_bus_islanded],
    include_base=True,
)

# Per-scenario result DataFrames
print(study.compare_buses())     # EPR per bus, with delta vs. base
print(study.compare_branches())  # branch currents, with delta vs. base

docs.title: The comparison frames
docs.text: compare_buses() and compare_branches() are long frames: one row per element, frequency, metric (EPR_V and I_bus_A for a bus, I_branch_A for a branch) and scenario, with the columns bus_name or branch_name, frequency_Hz, metric, value, scenario and the two delta columns. Unlike in res_buses, where the frequency is a number and the RMS row is marked by is_rms, frequency_Hz is text here: "50.0" for a frequency and "RMS" for the RMS value of the element. Filter with strings — pl.col("frequency_Hz") == "RMS", pl.col("frequency_Hz") == "50.0" — and keep the RMS rows out of anything that sums or averages over frequencies. The column tables are in Result tables.

docs.title: Reading the two delta columns
docs.text:
Each comparison carries an absolute delta_vs_<ref> and a relative delta_pct_vs_<ref>. The relative one is null wherever the reference value is zero, and that is the ordinary case rather than an exotic one:

situation reference scenario delta_vs_base delta_pct_vs_base a frequency the fault does not excite 0 V 0 V 0 V null a station islanded in the reference scenario 0 V 57.9 V 57.9 V null ordinary change 800 V 720 V −80 V −10 %

"Ten per cent of nothing" has no answer, so none is reported. A zero baseline arises from a scalings={250.0: 0.0} fault, from comparing against= a scenario that islands the bus in question, and from any element that carries no current in the reference — none of which is an error.

The absolute column keeps the full information in all three rows, so it is the one to rank by when a zero baseline is possible. And because the marker is null and not NaN, Polars aggregations skip it:

# fragment: continues the study above
tbl = study.compare_buses()
rms_epr = tbl.filter((pl.col("frequency_Hz") == "RMS") & (pl.col("metric") == "EPR_V"))
rms_epr["delta_pct_vs_base"].mean()   # finite; the null rows are skipped
tbl.filter(pl.col("delta_pct_vs_base").is_null())   # the zero-baseline rows

Use outage_context(network, outage) directly when a single one-off modification is needed:

# fragment: continues the example above
with gi.outage_context(net, scenario_cable_out):
    gi.run_fault(network=net, fault="fault1")
    print(net.res_all_impedances())
# net is fully restored on exit — including the cached paths.

docs.title: outage
docs.text:
Outage / What-If Study Module.

Convenience layer on top of the active flag of :class:groundinsight.models.core_models.Bus and :class:groundinsight.models.core_models.Branch. An :class:Outage is a named scenario that lists buses and/or branches to be deactivated; the :func:outage_context context manager applies the scenario for the duration of a with block and restores the previous state on exit, and :func:run_outage_study runs run_fault for the base case and a list of scenarios in one go and packages the results into an :class:OutageStudyResult with ready-made comparison helpers.

Example (net is a network that already carries a fault named "F1"):

>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> study = gi.run_outage_study(  # doctest: +SKIP
...     network=net,
...     fault="F1",
...     scenarios=[
...         gi.Outage(name="branch_b12_open", disabled_branches=["B12"]),
...         gi.Outage(name="bus5_isolated", disabled_buses=["bus5"]),
...     ],
... )
>>> df = study.compare_buses()            # doctest: +SKIP
>>> df_branch = study.compare_branches()  # doctest: +SKIP

Inactive elements are physically modelled as open circuits / removed nodes in the solver (see :mod:groundinsight.electrical_network and :mod:groundinsight.pathfinder); the outage layer does not duplicate that logic, it only flips the active flag and re-runs the existing run_fault pipeline.

>>> outage = gi.Outage(name="no_bus2", disabled_buses=["bus2"])

...     net.buses["bus2"].active

>>> net.buses["bus2"].active

Label of the base scenario (typically "base").

...     scenarios=[gi.Outage(name="no_bus2", disabled_buses=["bus2"])])
>>> study.labels()
['base', 'no_bus2']

def labels(self) -> List[str]:
    """
    Return the labels of all stored scenarios.

    The base label is included first (if present), followed by the user
    scenarios in the order they were submitted to ``run_outage_study``.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        Scenario labels.
    """
    order = []
    if self.base_label in self.bus_results:
        order.append(self.base_label)
    for scenario in self.scenarios:
        if scenario.name in self.bus_results:
            order.append(scenario.name)
    return order

outage_context(
    network: Network, outage: Outage
) -> Iterator[Network]

Apply an :class:Outage to network for the duration of a with block.

On entry, the active flag of the listed buses and branches is set to False. On exit, the original active values are restored even if the body raises. Path information is invalidated on entry and on exit because both the outage and its rollback can change topology.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default network Network

The network to mutate in place.

required outage Outage

Scenario describing what to deactivate.

required

Yields:

Type Description Network

The same network instance, mutated for the scenario.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a name in disabled_buses or disabled_branches is not part of the network.

Notes
  • The network's path-search memo (network.path_cache(), see :mod:groundinsight.pathfinder) is cleared on exit as well as on entry. Without the exit-side eviction, a multi-scenario outage sweep was accumulating one cache entry per scenario indefinitely; together with the LRU cap the cache footprint now matches the user-visible state of network.
  • The function is nestable. Each level snapshots the active flag of the elements it touches immediately before flipping them, and its exit reverts exactly those. An inner block therefore does not capture the already-modified outer state as its own baseline, and changes an inner block made to elements the outer one does not list survive the outer unwind. The snapshot is a plain local of this generator, which is all the nesting needs -- an earlier revision also pushed it onto a module-level _OUTAGE_BASELINE_STACK keyed by id(network) that nothing ever read back, and that carried a real risk: CPython reuses id() after garbage collection, so the key of a collected network could silently name a different one.

Examples:

Take bus2 out of service for one solve; the network is restored on leaving the block:

>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
>>> net = build_minimal()
>>> with gi.outage_context(net, gi.Outage(name="no_bus2", disabled_buses=["bus2"])):
...     result = gi.run_fault(net, "fault")
>>> net.buses["bus2"].active, [bus.name for bus in result.buses]
(True, ['bus1', 'bus3'])

@contextmanager
def outage_context(network: Network, outage: Outage) -> Iterator[Network]:
    """
    Apply an :class:`Outage` to ``network`` for the duration of a ``with`` block.

    On entry, the ``active`` flag of the listed buses and branches is set
    to ``False``. On exit, the original ``active`` values are restored
    even if the body raises. Path information is invalidated on entry and
    on exit because both the outage and its rollback can change topology.

    Parameters
    ----------
    network : Network
        The network to mutate in place.
    outage : Outage
        Scenario describing what to deactivate.

    Yields
    ------
    Network
        The same ``network`` instance, mutated for the scenario.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a name in ``disabled_buses`` or ``disabled_branches`` is not
        part of the network.

    Notes
    -----
    - The network's path-search memo (``network.path_cache()``, see
      :mod:`groundinsight.pathfinder`) is cleared **on exit** as well
      as on entry. Without the exit-side eviction, a multi-scenario
      outage sweep was accumulating one cache entry per scenario
      indefinitely; together with the LRU cap the cache footprint
      now matches the user-visible state of ``network``.
    - The function is **nestable**. Each level snapshots the ``active``
      flag of the elements *it* touches immediately before flipping
      them, and its exit reverts exactly those. An inner block
      therefore does not capture the already-modified outer state as
      its own baseline, and changes an inner block made to elements
      the outer one does not list survive the outer unwind. The
      snapshot is a plain local of this generator, which is all the
      nesting needs -- an earlier revision also pushed it onto a
      module-level ``_OUTAGE_BASELINE_STACK`` keyed by ``id(network)``
      that nothing ever read back, and that carried a real risk: CPython
      reuses ``id()`` after garbage collection, so the key of a
      collected network could silently name a different one.

    Examples
    --------
    Take ``bus2`` out of service for one solve; the network is restored on
    leaving the block:

    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
    >>> net = build_minimal()
    >>> with gi.outage_context(net, gi.Outage(name="no_bus2", disabled_buses=["bus2"])):
    ...     result = gi.run_fault(net, "fault")
    >>> net.buses["bus2"].active, [bus.name for bus in result.buses]
    (True, ['bus1', 'bus3'])
    """
    from groundinsight.pathfinder import clear_pathfinder_cache  # local import

    unknown_buses = [b for b in outage.disabled_buses if b not in network.buses]
    if unknown_buses:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Outage '{outage.name}' references unknown buses: {unknown_buses}"
        )
    unknown_branches = [
        b for b in outage.disabled_branches if b not in network.branches
    ]
    if unknown_branches:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Outage '{outage.name}' references unknown branches: {unknown_branches}"
        )

    # Nestable baseline tracking. Snapshot the pre-flip state for *this*
    # level, *before* mutating, so an outer level that has already flipped a
    # flag to ``False`` does not see the inner level "restore" it to ``False``
    # on exit: each level only reverts what it itself changed, at the moment
    # it changed it. That is the whole mechanism -- the generator frame of
    # each nested ``with`` holds its own ``level_baseline``, so the nesting is
    # the Python call stack and needs no bookkeeping of its own.
    level_baseline = {
        "buses": {
            name: network.buses[name].active for name in outage.disabled_buses
        },
        "branches": {
            name: network.branches[name].active
            for name in outage.disabled_branches
        },
    }

    saved_paths = dict(network.paths)

    try:
        for name in outage.disabled_buses:
            network.buses[name].active = False
        for name in outage.disabled_branches:
            network.branches[name].active = False
        # The pre-existing path cache is no longer valid for the new
        # topology — drop both ``network.paths`` and the module-level
        # pathfinder cache for this network so the inner solve rebuilds
        # both. Atomic rebind keeps any external snapshot intact.
        network.paths = {}
        clear_pathfinder_cache(network)
        yield network
    finally:
        # Restore only what *this* level touched.
        for name, value in level_baseline["buses"].items():
            network.buses[name].active = value
        for name, value in level_baseline["branches"].items():
            network.branches[name].active = value
        network.paths = saved_paths
        # Drop the cache entries this context built up so the resident
        # footprint matches the externally-visible state of ``network``.
        clear_pathfinder_cache(network)
