def __init__(
    self,
    network: gi.Network,
    *,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    store: Optional[ProjectStore] = None,
    key: Optional[str] = None,
    runner: Optional[JobRunner] = None,
    max_buses: Optional[int] = None,
    max_branches: Optional[int] = None,
    max_job_runtime_s: Optional[float] = None,
    max_undo: Optional[int] = 500,
    max_paths: Optional[int] = None,
) -> None:
    if not isinstance(network, gi.Network):
        raise TypeError(f"a session holds a groundinsight.Network, got {type(network).__name__}")
    if path is not None and store is not None:
        raise ValueError("a project lives in a file or in a store, not both")
    if (store is None) != (key is None):
        raise ValueError("a store location needs both store and key")
    self._limits = SessionLimitsDTO(
        max_buses=max_buses,
        max_branches=max_branches,
        max_job_runtime_s=max_job_runtime_s,
        max_undo=max_undo,
        max_paths=max_paths,
    )
    _check_size(network, self._limits)
    if self._limits.max_paths is not None:
        # Runtime settings of this network only: kept by the job snapshots
        # (copies and pickles keep them), not written to the project file.
        network.pathfinder_settings = gi.PathfinderSettings(
            max_paths=self._limits.max_paths,
            cache_size=network.pathfinder_settings.cache_size,
        )
    network.to_tables()  # refuses two different types of the same name
    self._network = network
    self._path = str(path) if path is not None else None
    self._store = store
    self._key = key
    self._bus_types = _catalogue(network.buses.values())
    self._branch_types = _catalogue(network.branches.values())
    self._lock = threading.RLock()
    self._revision = 0
    self._saved_revision = 0
    self._revisions = itertools.count(1)
    self._done: List[_Entry] = []
    self._undone: List[_Entry] = []
    self._runner = runner
    self._owns_runner = runner is None
    self._sequence = itertools.count(1)
    self._result_sequence: Dict[str, int] = {}
    self._result_revision: Dict[str, Optional[int]] = {}
    self._result_mode: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
    self._handles: List[JobHandle] = []
    self._closed = False

def apply(self, command: Union[Command, Dict[str, Any]]) -> CommandResultDTO:
    """
    Apply an edit command and record it for undo.

    Parameters
    ----------
    command : Command or dict
        The command, or its JSON form (see
        :func:`~groundinsight.api.commands.parse_command`). The session
        applies a copy, so one command object can be applied to several
        sessions.

    Returns
    -------
    CommandResultDTO
        The new revision, the library warnings the command raised (a
        frequency order, a source value outside the network frequencies),
        the stale results and the history state.

    Raises
    ------
    CommandError
        If the command is rejected; network, catalogue, revision and
        history are unchanged.
    """
    command = parse_command(command).model_copy(deep=True)
    with self._lock:
        self._require_open()
        paths_before = self._network.paths
        with collecting() as records:
            command.apply(self._context())
        entry = _Entry(command, self._revision, next(self._revisions), paths_before)
        self._done.append(entry)
        self._undone.clear()
        limit = self._limits.max_undo
        if limit is not None and len(self._done) > limit:
            del self._done[: len(self._done) - limit]
        self._revision = entry.after
        return self._command_result(command, records)

def close(self) -> None:
    """
    Cancel this session's jobs and shut down its own runner.

    A runner passed to the constructor is left running (it may serve
    other sessions); jobs of this session on it are cancelled.
    """
    with self._lock:
        if self._closed:
            return
        self._closed = True
        runner = self._runner
        handles = list(self._handles)
    if runner is None:
        return
    if self._owns_runner:
        runner.shutdown(wait=True)
        return
    for handle in handles:
        handle.cancel()

    """
    Open a project file (:func:`groundinsight.load_network_from_json`).

    ----------

    try:

def redo(self) -> Optional[CommandResultDTO]:
    """
    Apply the last undone command again.

    Returns
    -------
    CommandResultDTO or None
        The command and the session state afterwards; ``None`` when there
        is nothing to redo.
    """
    with self._lock:
        self._require_open()
        if not self._undone:
            return None
        entry = self._undone.pop()
        entry.paths = self._network.paths
        with collecting() as records:
            entry.command.apply(self._context())
        self._done.append(entry)
        self._revision = entry.after
        return self._command_result(entry.command, records)

def result(self, fault: str) -> Optional[FaultResultDTO]:
    """
    The stored result of a fault, as a DTO.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fault : str
        The fault.

    Returns
    -------

        ``None`` when no result is stored. ``revision`` is the revision
        the result was computed from (``None`` for one that came with the
        project file); ``stale`` is the library's verdict now.
    """
    with self._lock:
        if fault not in self._network.results or fault not in self._network.faults:
            return None
        return fault_result_dto(
            self._network,
            fault,
            revision=self._result_revision.get(fault),
            phase_current_mode=self._result_mode.get(fault),
            stale=self._network.is_result_stale(fault),
        )

def save(self, path: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Save the project -- to ``path`` ("save as") or to its location.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : str, optional
        A project file. Without it, the session's file or store location.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The location saved to (:attr:`location`).

    Raises
    ------
    ProjectError
        If there is no location, or writing fails; an existing file is
        then unchanged (the library writes atomically) and the session
        stays dirty.
    """
    with self._lock:
        self._require_open()
        if path is None and self._path is None and self._store is None:
            raise ProjectError("the project has no location yet; pass a path")
        view = _without_results(self._network)
        if path is not None or self._store is None:
            target = str(path) if path is not None else self._path
            try:
                gi.save_network_to_json(view, target)
            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise ProjectError(f"cannot save '{target}': {rejection_reason(exc)}") from exc
            self._path, self._store, self._key = target, None, None
        else:
            self._save_to_store(self._store, self._key, view)
        self._saved_revision = self._revision
        return self.location

def save_to(self, store: ProjectStore, key: str) -> str:

    Save the project into a store ("save as"); the store becomes its location.

    store : ProjectStore
        The store.

        The project key.

    -------
    str
        ``"<scheme>:<key>"``.

    Raises

    ProjectError
        If the store refuses the project.

        self._require_open()

def solve(self, fault: str, *, phase_current_mode: str = "auto") -> FaultResultDTO:
    """
    Solve one fault in the calling thread and store the result.

    For scripts and the command-line interface. A user interface uses
    :meth:`submit_solve`, which keeps its event loop free.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fault : str
        The fault.
    phase_current_mode : {"auto", "paths"}
        As in :func:`groundinsight.run_fault`.

    Returns
    -------
    FaultResultDTO
        The result, bound to the current revision.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Whatever :func:`groundinsight.solve` raises (unknown fault, no
        source, a network the solver rejects).
    """
    request = SolveRequestDTO(fault=fault, phase_current_mode=phase_current_mode)
    with self._lock:
        self._require_open()
        snapshot = snapshot_network(self._network)
        revision = self._revision
        sequence = next(self._sequence)
    outcome = run_task(request, snapshot, revision=revision)
    return self._bind(outcome, sequence, revision, request)

def submit(self, request: Any) -> JobHandle:
    """
    Run a job request off the caller's thread.

    Parameters
    ----------
    request : job request DTO or dict
        A :class:`~groundinsight.api.schemas.SolveRequestDTO`,
        ``SolveAllRequestDTO``, ``SweepRequestDTO``,
        ``OutageStudyRequestDTO`` or ``MaxRhoRequestDTO``, or its JSON
        form.

    Returns
    -------
    JobHandle
        Poll :meth:`JobHandle.status`, wait with :meth:`JobHandle.result`,
        stop with :meth:`JobHandle.cancel`. Fault results are stored on
        the network when the job finishes (see the module docstring).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the request is invalid.
    RuntimeError
        If the session is closed.
    """
    request = parse_job_request(request)
    with self._lock:
        self._require_open()
        snapshot = snapshot_network(self._network)
        revision = self._revision
        sequence = next(self._sequence)
    handle = self.runner.submit(
        request,
        snapshot,
        revision=revision,
        max_runtime_s=self._limits.max_job_runtime_s,
        on_success=lambda outcome: self._bind(outcome, sequence, revision, request),
        copy_network=False,
    )
    with self._lock:
        self._handles = [h for h in self._handles if not h.done]
        self._handles.append(handle)
    return handle

def summary(self) -> NetworkSummaryDTO:
    """
    What a header bar shows: name, counts, history and save state.

    -------

        The summary.

    with self._lock:

        return NetworkSummaryDTO(
            name=network.name,
            description=network.description,
            frequencies=[float(f) for f in network.frequencies],
            n_buses=len(network.buses),
            n_branches=len(network.branches),
            n_sources=len(network.sources),
            n_faults=len(network.faults),
            bus_types=list(self._bus_types),
            branch_types=list(self._branch_types),
            faults=list(network.faults),
            results=list(network.results),
            stale_results=network.stale_results(),
            revision=self._revision,
            dirty=self.dirty,
            can_undo=bool(self._done),
            can_redo=bool(self._undone),
            undo_label=self._done[-1].command.label if self._done else None,
            redo_label=self._undone[-1].command.label if self._undone else None,
            location=self.location,

def undo(self) -> Optional[CommandResultDTO]:
    """
    Revert the last applied command.

    Returns
    -------
    CommandResultDTO or None
        The reverted command and the session state afterwards; ``None``
        when there is nothing to undo.
    """
    with self._lock:
        self._require_open()
        if not self._done:
            return None
        entry = self._done[-1]
        try:
            with collecting() as records:
                entry.command.revert(self._context())
                if self._network.paths is not entry.paths:
                    self._network.paths = entry.paths
        except Exception:
            # Reverting restores a state the library accepted before, so
            # this is a defect, not a user error: keep the entry; the
            # exception reaches the caller.
            logger.debug("undo of '%s' failed", entry.command.label, exc_info=True)
            raise
        self._done.pop()
        self._undone.append(entry)
        self._revision = entry.before
        return self._command_result(entry.command, records)

docs.title: commands
docs.text:
Edit commands: every change of a project, atomic and undoable.

A front end never assigns to a model field itself. It builds a command -- UpdateBus(name="b1", fields={"specific_earth_resistance": 250.0}) -- and hands it to :meth:ProjectSession.apply <groundinsight.api.ProjectSession.apply>. Three properties hold for every command:

It goes through the library. A command calls the library's own editing API -- Network.add_*, update_bus, update_branch, remove_*, assignment of Network.frequencies and of attached elements' fields -- which validates the input, re-derives the impedances through the same code path as create_bus and keeps the network's invariants (no dangling bus reference, no rename of an attached element). The command adds no physics and no second validation that could disagree with the library's.

It is atomic. A rejected command raises :class:CommandError and leaves the network, the session's type catalogue, the revision and the history exactly as they were. The library methods are atomic themselves; where a command needs several of them (a type edit re-derives every element of that type), it rolls back the steps already done before it re-raises.

It is undoable. Undo runs inverse operations through the same library API -- remove_bus undoes add_bus and vice versa -- rather than restoring a snapshot of the whole network, which would cost a deep copy of every impedance table per keystroke. What a library call drops as a side effect is put back explicitly: the stored result and the active state of a removed fault, the position of a re-added element in its dictionary, and derived values the user had overridden by assignment. The session tests check the outcome the strict way: after undo, the serialised network is identical to the one before the command, so a result computed before the command is current again (the library compares input digests by content).

Types. BusType and BranchType are read-only in the library: a type is evaluated into every element that uses it, so a changed type is a new type, swapped into its users with update_bus/update_branch. Elements refer to types by name in the tables a front end edits, so the session keeps a catalogue of types by name -- the types in use plus types added for later use -- and the type commands edit it. All of that lives in :class:_TypeCommand: should the maintainer decide that editing a type re-derives its users in place, only that class changes.

The commands are pydantic models with a discriminator field op, so they are also the request bodies of a future REST endpoint; :func:parse_command builds one from its JSON form.

def apply(self, context: CommandContext) -> None:
    """
    Apply the command.

    Parameters
    ----------
    context : CommandContext
        Network, type catalogue and limits of the session.

    Raises
    ------
    CommandError
        If the library rejects the change; nothing has changed then.
    """
    try:
        self._apply(context)
    except CommandError:
        raise
    except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError) as exc:
        raise CommandError(f"{self.label}: {rejection_reason(exc)}") from exc

    self._revert(context)

def check_room(self, collection: str) -> None:
    """
    Refuse one more element beyond the session's size limit.

    Parameters
    ----------
    collection : {"buses", "branches"}
        The element collection that is about to grow by one.

    Raises
    ------
    CommandError
        If the collection already holds ``max_buses``/``max_branches``
        elements.
    """
    limit_name = {"buses": "max_buses", "branches": "max_branches"}[collection]
    limit = getattr(self.limits, limit_name)
    size = len(getattr(self.network, collection))
    if limit is not None and size >= limit:
        raise CommandError(
            f"the network already has {size} {collection}; this session "
            f"allows at most {limit} ({limit_name})"
        )

def type_named(self, kind: str, name: Any):
    """
    Look up a type of the catalogue by name.

    Parameters
    ----------
    kind : {"bus", "branch"}
        The element kind.
    name : str
        The type name.

    Returns
    -------
    BusType or BranchType
        The catalogue's type object.

    Raises
    ------
    CommandError
        If ``name`` is not a string or names no type of the catalogue.
    """
    catalogue = self.catalogue(kind)
    if not isinstance(name, str):
        raise CommandError(
            f"a {kind} type is referred to by its name, got {type(name).__name__}"
        )
    if name not in catalogue:
        raise CommandError(
            f"{kind} type '{name}' is not in the catalogue "
            f"(known: {', '.join(sorted(catalogue)) or 'none'})"
        )
    return catalogue[name]

Change fields of a source, all or nothing.

The library has no update_source: a source's fields depend on each other (source_type decides which of values/voltage must be set), so they cannot be assigned one by one. def parse_command(data: Any) -> Command:
    """
    Build a command from its JSON form.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : dict or Command
        A mapping with an ``op`` key, or a command, which is returned as is.

    Returns
    -------
    Command
        The command object.

    Raises
    ------
    CommandError
        If ``op`` names no command or a field is missing or invalid.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> parse_command({"op": "remove_bus", "name": "b7"}).label
    "remove bus 'b7'"
    """
    if isinstance(data, Command):
        return data
    op = data.get("op") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if op not in COMMAND_OPS:
        raise CommandError(
            f"unknown command op {op!r}; known ops: {', '.join(COMMAND_OPS)}"
        )
    try:
        return COMMAND_ADAPTER.validate_python(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise CommandError(f"invalid '{op}' command: {rejection_reason(exc)}") from exc

def rejection_reason(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    """
    The library's reason for a rejection, as a front end shows it.

    Internal API: the session words its project errors with it, too; not
    exported, may change in any release.

    A pydantic ``ValidationError`` renders as a multi-line report (error
    count, model name, input echo, a link to pydantic's documentation) around
    the one sentence the library wrote. Front ends show the reason verbatim,
    so only the messages are kept, each with its field when the message does
    not name it already.

    Parameters
    ----------
    exc : BaseException
        The exception the library raised.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        One line per message, joined with ``"; "``.
    """
    if not isinstance(exc, ValidationError):
        return str(exc)
    parts = []
    for error in exc.errors(include_url=False):
        message = str(error.get("msg", "")).removeprefix("Value error, ")
        location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
        parts.append(f"{location}: {message}" if location and location not in message else message)
    return "; ".join(parts) or str(exc)

docs.title: jobs
docs.text:
Jobs: library work off the caller's thread, with progress, cancel and limits.

A user interface has one rule for long work: the event loop that draws the window never waits for a solve. A server has a second one: one user's study must not run forever on a shared machine. :class:JobRunner serves both. It runs a job request (:mod:groundinsight.api.schemas, task = "solve", "solve_all", "sweep", "outage", "max_rho") on a network copy in a worker and hands back a :class:JobHandle that a UI timer or an HTTP handler polls (:meth:JobHandle.status is a plain DTO).

Two backends, one computation

backend="thread" (default) runs the task in a worker thread of this process: no start-up cost, the right choice for a fault solve that takes milliseconds to seconds and spends its time in NumPy/SciPy. backend="process" pickles the request and the network copy into a freshly spawned process: it costs the interpreter start (about a second) and needs inputs that pickle (a network does), and in return the job can be stopped hard and cannot take the caller's process down. Both run the same task function of :mod:groundinsight.api.tasks on equal inputs, and the tests compare their DTOs field by field.

Progress, cancel, runtime limit

Progress and cancellation use the library's study hooks: progress(done, total, label) is forwarded into the handle (from a child process through a pipe), and should_cancel() answers true once :meth:JobHandle.cancel was called or the runtime limit has passed. The study then raises :class:groundinsight.StudyCancelled at its next unit boundary and the job ends "cancelled" or "timeout" -- with no partial result. Cancellation is cooperative in a thread, because Python cannot stop a thread from outside: a single solve, which has no hook inside, runs to its end and its result is then discarded. In a process the runner asks the same way first and terminates the process if it has not stopped cancel_grace_s later, so a process job never runs much beyond its limit. A queued job that is cancelled never starts.

A job either completes ("done", with its DTO) or it does not ("cancelled", "timeout", "failed") -- a result that arrives after its cancel request or its limit is not delivered. A failure is data (:class:~groundinsight.api.schemas.JobErrorDTO: exception type and message), never an exception in the polling thread; :meth:JobHandle.result re-raises it as :class:JobFailed for code that waits.

The runner keeps no state outside its instances; a server may share one runner between sessions (each job carries its own limit) or give each session its own.

Source code in src/groundinsight/api/jobs.py 
def cancel(self) -> bool:
    """
    Ask the job to stop.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        ``True`` if the job will not complete: a queued job is cancelled
        at once, a running one stops at its next unit boundary (a process
        is terminated if it does not). ``False`` if it has already ended.
    """
    with self._lock:
        if self._state in FINAL_STATES:
            return False
        self._cancel.set()
        if self._state == "queued":
            self._state = "cancelled"
            self._finished = time.monotonic()
            self._ended.set()
        return True

def result(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> Any:
    """
    Wait for the job and return its DTO.

    Parameters
    ----------
    timeout : float, optional
        Seconds to wait; ``None`` waits indefinitely.

    Returns
    -------
    BaseModel
        The result DTO of a ``"done"`` job.

    Raises
    ------
    TimeoutError
        If the job has not ended within ``timeout``.
    JobTimeout
        If the runtime limit stopped it.
    JobCancelled
        If it was cancelled.
    JobFailed
        If it raised; ``__cause__`` is the original exception where
        available.
    """
    if not self._ended.wait(timeout):
        raise TimeoutError(f"job {self.job_id} ({self.label}) has not ended yet")
    with self._lock:
        state, error, exception, result = self._state, self._error, self._exception, self._result
        progress = self._progress
    if state == "done":
        return result
    if state == "timeout":
        raise JobTimeout(
            f"job {self.job_id} ({self.label}) exceeded its runtime limit of "
            f"{self.max_runtime_s} s",
            done=progress.done,
            total=progress.total,
        )
    if state == "cancelled":
        raise JobCancelled(
            f"job {self.job_id} ({self.label}) was cancelled",
            done=progress.done,
            total=progress.total,
        )
    message = f"job {self.job_id} ({self.label}) failed: {error.type}: {error.message}"
    raise JobFailed(message, error_type=error.type, error_message=error.message) from exception

def status(self) -> JobStatusDTO:
    """
    A JSON-safe snapshot of the job.

    Returns
    -------
    JobStatusDTO
        State, progress, timing and error.
    """
    with self._lock:
        elapsed = None
        if self._started is not None:
            elapsed = (self._finished or time.monotonic()) - self._started
        return JobStatusDTO(
            job_id=self.job_id,
            task=self.task,
            label=self.label,
            backend=self.backend,
            state=self._state,
            revision=self.revision,
            progress=self._progress,
            elapsed_s=elapsed,
            max_runtime_s=self.max_runtime_s,
            error=self._error,
        )

def __init__(
    self,
    backend: str = "thread",
    *,
    max_workers: int = 1,
    max_runtime_s: Optional[float] = None,
    cancel_grace_s: float = 5.0,
    poll_interval_s: float = 0.05,
    keep_finished: int = 200,
) -> None:
    if backend not in ("thread", "process"):
        raise ValueError(f"backend must be 'thread' or 'process', got {backend!r}")
    if not isinstance(max_workers, int) or max_workers < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_workers must be a positive integer, got {max_workers!r}")
    self.backend = backend
    self.max_runtime_s = max_runtime_s
    self.cancel_grace_s = float(cancel_grace_s)
    self.poll_interval_s = float(poll_interval_s)
    self.keep_finished = int(keep_finished)
    self._executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers, thread_name_prefix="gi-job")
    self._jobs: Dict[str, JobHandle] = {}
    self._lock = threading.Lock()
    self._closed = False
    self._counter = itertools.count(1)

def shutdown(self, wait: bool = True) -> None:
    """
    Cancel every job that has not ended and stop the workers.

    Parameters
    ----------
    wait : bool
        Wait until running jobs have stopped.
    """
    with self._lock:
        self._closed = True
        handles = list(self._jobs.values())
    for handle in handles:
        handle.cancel()
    self._executor.shutdown(wait=wait, cancel_futures=True)

def submit(
    self,
    request: Any,
    network: gi.Network,
    *,
    label: Optional[str] = None,
    revision: Optional[int] = None,
    max_runtime_s: Optional[float] = None,
    on_success: Optional[Callable[[TaskOutcome], Any]] = None,
    copy_network: bool = True,
) -> JobHandle:
    """
    Queue a job.

    Parameters
    ----------
    request : job request DTO or dict
        What to compute (:func:`~groundinsight.api.schemas.parse_job_request`).
    network : Network
        The network to compute on.
    label : str, optional
        Description for the status; default ``"<task> <fault>"``.
    revision : int, optional
        Session revision of ``network``, written into the DTOs.
    max_runtime_s : float, optional
        This job's runtime limit; default the runner's.
    on_success : callable, optional
        Called in the worker with the :class:`TaskOutcome` of a completed
        job; its return value becomes the job's result (the session uses
        it to store fault results on its network). Default: the outcome's
        DTO.
    copy_network : bool
        Compute on a snapshot (:func:`snapshot_network`) instead of
        ``network`` itself. Default ``True``; pass ``False`` only for a
        network the caller no longer touches.

    Returns
    -------
    JobHandle
        The job.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        If the runner has been shut down.
    ValueError
        If the request is invalid.
    """
    request = parse_job_request(request)
    if copy_network:
        network = snapshot_network(network)
    limit = max_runtime_s if max_runtime_s is not None else self.max_runtime_s
    fault = getattr(request, "fault", None)
    text = label or (f"{request.task} {fault}" if fault else request.task)
    job_id = f"{next(self._counter)}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
    handle = JobHandle(job_id, request, self.backend, revision, limit, text)
    with self._lock:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("the job runner has been shut down")
        self._jobs[job_id] = handle
        self._forget_old()
        worker = self._run_in_process if self.backend == "process" else self._run_in_thread
        self._executor.submit(worker, handle, network, on_success)
    return handle

docs.title: snapshot_network
docs.text:
snapshot_network(network: Network) -> gi.Network

An independent copy of a network's inputs, for a job to compute on.

copy.deepcopy with a memo that maps the stored results and the enumerated paths to empty dictionaries skips both: they are the bulk of a solved network and a solve needs neither (empty paths are rebuilt on demand). The copy's elements are attached to the copy, so a study that edits it re-derives correctly, and a result computed on it carries the same input digest as one computed on the original.

Parameters:

def snapshot_network(network: gi.Network) -> gi.Network:
    """
    An independent copy of a network's inputs, for a job to compute on.

    ``copy.deepcopy`` with a memo that maps the stored results and the
    enumerated paths to empty dictionaries skips both: they are the bulk of a
    solved network and a solve needs neither (empty paths are rebuilt on
    demand). The copy's elements are attached to the copy, so a study that
    edits it re-derives correctly, and a result computed on it carries the
    same input digest as one computed on the original.

    Parameters
    ----------
    network : Network
        The network.

    Returns
    -------
    Network
        The copy.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> net = gi.create_network(name="n", frequencies=[50.0])
    >>> copy_ = snapshot_network(net)
    >>> copy_ is net, copy_.name
    (False, 'n')
    """
    memo = {id(network.results): {}, id(network.paths): {}}
    return copy.deepcopy(network, memo)

docs.title: schemas
docs.text:
Data transfer objects (DTOs) between the service layer and a front end.

They are the only data shape that crosses that boundary.

A front end -- the NiceGUI app, the command-line interface, a later REST server and its web client -- must not reach into :class:~groundinsight.Network or the Result models to draw something. Those are the library's working objects: they carry ComplexNumber phasors, frequency-keyed dictionaries and private solver state, and their shape follows the physics. A screen that picks numbers out of them is where "physics in the GUI" starts (a wrong field, a magnitude taken of the wrong phasor). The models in this module are what a front end gets instead, and they are deliberately plain:

  • Strictly JSON-safe. Every value is str, bool, int, a finite float, None, or a list/dict of those. A non-finite number -- the infinite impedance of an open end (formula "nan"), an undefined ratio -- becomes None when the DTO is built, in Python as well as in JSON: a browser's JSON.parse rejects NaN and Infinity, and a None cannot be mistaken for a number by a template either.
  • Versioned. Every DTO carries dto_schema_version (:data:DTO_SCHEMA_VERSION). A change that a reader of the previous version would misread increments it; a validator refuses a DTO of another version instead of guessing.
  • Schemas of a REST API. The DTOs are pydantic models, so they are the request and response schemas of a future HTTP layer as they stand: :func:json_schemas returns the JSON schema of every DTO, of the edit commands (:mod:groundinsight.api.commands, one discriminated union keyed by op) and of the job requests (keyed by task).
  • Tables are tables. A table is a list of columns plus a list of row dictionaries keyed by column name -- what an AG Grid, a CSV writer and a test assertion all consume without an adapter. The element tables use the pinned schema of :meth:Network.to_tables <groundinsight.Network.to_tables>, the result tables those of res_buses/res_branches, and the key figures the columns of :meth:Network.res_fault <groundinsight.Network.res_fault> -- the same names a notebook sees.

Rejected alternatives: handing out Polars frames (a frame is not a wire format, and a front end holding one starts deriving numbers from it), and exposing the pydantic result models (couples every screen to the library's internal model and its ComplexNumber encoding).

def finite_or_none(value: Any) -> Optional[float]:
    """
    A number as a finite ``float``, or ``None`` when that is impossible.

    Parameters
    ----------
    value : Any
        A number (``int``, ``float``, NumPy scalar), ``None``, or anything
        else.

    Returns
    -------
    Optional[float]
        ``float(value)`` when it is finite; ``None`` for ``None``, for
        ``NaN``/``inf``, and for a value that is not a number.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> finite_or_none(1.5)
    1.5
    >>> finite_or_none(float("inf")) is None, finite_or_none(None) is None
    (True, True)
    """
    if value is None or isinstance(value, bool):
        return None
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return number if math.isfinite(number) else None

def json_schemas() -> Dict[str, dict]:
    """
    The JSON schema of every DTO, of the commands and of the job requests.

    These are the request and response schemas of a future REST API; a test
    checks that every DTO round-trips through JSON against them.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to dict
        DTO class name to its JSON schema, plus ``"Command"`` (the union of
        every edit command, discriminated by ``op``) and ``"JobRequest"``
        (the union of the job requests, discriminated by ``task``).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> schemas = json_schemas()
    >>> "dto_schema_version" in schemas["FaultResultDTO"]["properties"]
    True
    """
    from .commands import COMMAND_ADAPTER  # local: commands builds on this module

    schemas: Dict[str, dict] = {}
    for name in __all__:
        cls = globals()[name]
        if isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, BaseDTO):
            schemas[name] = cls.model_json_schema()
    schemas["Command"] = COMMAND_ADAPTER.json_schema()
    schemas["JobRequest"] = _JOB_REQUEST_ADAPTER.json_schema()
    return schemas

    Build a job request from its JSON form.

        ``"sweep"``, ``"outage"``, ``"max_rho"``), or a request DTO, which is
        returned unchanged.

docs.title: examples
docs.text:
The documented example networks, as project templates.

A user interface offers "new project from template", and the service-layer tests need networks whose numbers are documented. Both use the networks of the documentation, rebuilt here through the public API exactly as the pages build them:

  • "quickstart" -- the network of docs/getting-started/first-calculation.md (two substations, one cable), at five frequencies and with a fault whose scalings cover 50 Hz only;
  • "minimal" -- docs/examples/minimal.ipynb: a three-bus cable line at 50 Hz whose reduction factor has a closed form;
  • "mv_ring" -- docs/examples/mv_ring.ipynb: a 20-station 20 kV cable ring, 1 kA at 50 Hz fed at b01, fault F1 at b10.

Each builder returns a fresh, unsolved :class:~groundinsight.Network and touches no global state.

def build_minimal() -> gi.Network:
    """
    The three-bus cable line of the minimal example.

    Returns
    -------
    Network
        ``SmokeTest``: ``bus1``-``bus2``-``bus3`` with 1 km cables ``b12`` and
        ``b23``, 100 A at 50 Hz fed at ``bus1``, fault ``fault`` at ``bus3``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> net = build_minimal()
    >>> list(net.branches), net.frequencies
    (['b12', 'b23'], [50.0])
    """
    net = gi.create_network(
        name="SmokeTest", frequencies=[50], description="3-bus MV-cable line, single frequency"
    )
    bus_type = gi.BusType(
        name="BusUnit",
        description="Unit-like bus impedance for plausibility tests",
        system_type="Grounded",
        voltage_level=20.0,
        impedance_formula="rho * 0 + 1.0 + I * f * 0",
    )
    cable = gi.BranchType(
        name="MSCable",
        description="MV cable reference branch",
        grounding_conductor=True,
        self_impedance_formula="(rho * 0 + 0.25 + I * 0.6)*l",
        mutual_impedance_formula="(rho * 0 + 0.0 + I * 0.6)*l",
    )
    for i in range(1, 4):
        gi.create_bus(name=f"bus{i}", type=bus_type, network=net)
    gi.create_branch(name="b12", type=cable, from_bus="bus1", to_bus="bus2", length=1.0, network=net)
    gi.create_branch(name="b23", type=cable, from_bus="bus2", to_bus="bus3", length=1.0, network=net)
    gi.create_source(name="src", bus="bus1", values={50: 100.0}, network=net)
    gi.create_fault(name="fault", bus="bus3", scalings={50: 1.0}, network=net)
    return net

def build_mv_ring(n_buses: int = 20) -> gi.Network:
    """
    The 20 kV cable ring of the ``mv_ring`` example.

    Per section: NA2XS(F)2Y 1x300 RM/25, 0.5 km, ``R = 0.25 Ohm/km``,
    ``L = 1.9 mH/km``, Carson mutual ``0.05 Ohm/km + 1.85 mH/km``; every
    station 5 Ohm in parallel with the lumped cable capacitance (150 nF).

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_buses : int, optional
        Number of stations; the documented network has 20.

    Returns
    -------
    Network
        ``mv_ring_<n>`` at 50 Hz: buses ``b01`` ... , branches
        ``L_01_02`` ..., source ``src`` (1 kA at ``b01``), fault ``F1`` at
        the opposite station (``b10`` for 20 stations).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        For fewer than three stations.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> net = build_mv_ring()
    >>> len(net.buses), net.faults["F1"].bus
    (20, 'b10')
    """
    if n_buses < 3:
        raise ValueError(f"a ring needs at least 3 stations, got {n_buses}")
    r_per_km, l_per_km, c_per_km = 0.25, 1.9e-3, 300e-9
    r_mut_per_km, m_per_km = 0.05, 1.85e-3
    section_km, r_bus = 0.5, 5.0
    c_bus = c_per_km * section_km
    bus_type = gi.BusType(
        name="MV_substation",
        description="20 kV substation grounding, 5 ohm; cable C lumped automatically",
        system_type="Substation",
        voltage_level=20.0,
        impedance_formula=f"((rho * 0 + {r_bus}) / (1 + I * 2 * pi * f * {r_bus} * {c_bus}))",
        R_formula=f"rho * 0 + {r_bus}",
    )
    branch_type = gi.BranchType(
        name="NA2XS_300_25",
        description="NA2XS(F)2Y 1x300 RM/25 with Carson mutual coupling",
        grounding_conductor=True,
        self_impedance_formula=f"((rho * 0 + {r_per_km}) + I * 2 * pi * f * {l_per_km}) * l",
        mutual_impedance_formula=f"((rho * 0 + {r_mut_per_km}) + I * 2 * pi * f * {m_per_km}) * l",
        R_self_formula=f"({r_per_km}) * l",
        L_self_formula=f"({l_per_km}) * l",
        C_self_formula=f"({c_per_km}) * l",
        R_mutual_formula=f"({r_mut_per_km}) * l",
        M_mutual_formula=f"({m_per_km}) * l",
    )
    net = gi.create_network(name=f"mv_ring_{n_buses}", frequencies=[50.0])
    for k in range(1, n_buses + 1):
        gi.create_bus(name=f"b{k:02d}", type=bus_type, network=net)
    for k in range(1, n_buses + 1):
        nxt = (k % n_buses) + 1
        gi.create_branch(
            name=f"L_{k:02d}_{nxt:02d}",
            type=branch_type,
            from_bus=f"b{k:02d}",
            to_bus=f"b{nxt:02d}",
            length=section_km,
            network=net,
        )
    gi.create_source(name="src", bus="b01", values={50.0: 1000.0 + 0.0j}, network=net)
    gi.create_fault(name="F1", bus=f"b{n_buses // 2:02d}", scalings={50.0: 1.0}, network=net)
    return net

def build_quickstart() -> gi.Network:
    """
    The network of the first tutorial, at five frequencies.

    Returns
    -------
    Network
        ``QuickstartNet``: buses ``bus_source`` and ``bus_fault``, cable
        ``cable_1`` (5 km), source ``substation_infeed`` (1000 A at 50 Hz plus
        harmonics), fault ``fault_at_remote_bus``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> net = build_quickstart()
    >>> sorted(net.buses), list(net.faults)
    (['bus_fault', 'bus_source'], ['fault_at_remote_bus'])
    """
    net = gi.create_network(name="QuickstartNet", frequencies=[50, 250, 350, 450, 550])
    bus_type = gi.BusType(
        name="SubstationBus",
        description="Lumped substation grounding grid",
        system_type="Substation",
        voltage_level=20,
        impedance_formula="rho * 0.01 + j * f * 1/50 * 0.1",
    )
    cable_type = gi.BranchType(
        name="MSCable",
        description="20 kV single-core cable with shield",
        grounding_conductor=True,
        self_impedance_formula="(0.25 + j * f * 0.012) * l",
        mutual_impedance_formula="(0.0  + j * f * 0.012) * l",
    )
    for name in ("bus_source", "bus_fault"):
        gi.create_bus(name=name, type=bus_type, network=net, specific_earth_resistance=100.0)
    gi.create_branch(
        name="cable_1",
        type=cable_type,
        from_bus="bus_source",
        to_bus="bus_fault",
        length=5.0,
        specific_earth_resistance=100.0,
        network=net,
    )
    gi.create_source(
        name="substation_infeed",
        bus="bus_source",
        values={50: 1000.0, 250: 200.0, 350: 100.0, 450: 50.0, 550: 25.0},
        network=net,
    )
    gi.create_fault(
        name="fault_at_remote_bus",
        bus="bus_fault",
        description="Single-phase-to-ground fault at bus_fault",
        scalings={50: 1.0},
        network=net,
    )
    return net

docs.title: cli
docs.text:
The groundinsight command line: solve and check a project file.

::

groundinsight run projekt.json --fault F1 [--format table|json|csv]
groundinsight check projekt.json [--fault F1] [--format table|json|csv]
python -m groundinsight ...            # the same, without the script

Why a command line, and why first: it is the smallest front end that needs everything a GUI needs -- open a project, check it, solve a fault, report the key figures and the diagnostics -- so it is the first consumer of the service layer :mod:groundinsight.api and proves its shape before a window does. It is also what a batch job, a CI pipeline or a colleague without Python experience runs.

It is built on the service layer only (the same rule the GUI follows): a :class:~groundinsight.api.ProjectSession opens the file, check prints the pre-flight check, run checks, solves through the session and prints the :class:~groundinsight.api.FaultResultDTO. No number is computed here; the table and CSV outputs only format the DTO's key figures, which are the rows of :meth:Network.res_fault <groundinsight.Network.res_fault>.

Output formats

table (default) A readable report: the key figures per frequency and RMS, then every diagnostic with its elements. json The DTO as JSON (strict RFC 8259: no NaN/Infinity) -- :class:~groundinsight.api.FaultResultDTO for run, :class:~groundinsight.api.CheckReportDTO for check and for a run the pre-flight check stopped. csv run: the key-figure rows with the columns of :data:groundinsight.RES_FAULT_SCHEMA; check: one row per finding. Diagnostics of a run go to stderr, so stdout stays pure CSV.

Exit codes

0 Success. 1 A diagnostic of severity error: the pre-flight check found the network unsolvable as described (run then solves nothing), the solve itself failed, or the result carries an error record. 2 A usage error: invalid arguments, a project file that cannot be opened, an unknown fault, or run without --fault on a network with several faults.

def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    """
    Run the command line.

    Parameters
    ----------
    argv : list of str, optional
        The arguments without the program name; default ``sys.argv[1:]``.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The exit code (see the module docstring). Invalid arguments make
        ``argparse`` exit with code 2 itself.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> main(["--version"])  # doctest: +SKIP
    groundinsight 2026.11.0
    """
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    # The diagnostics are part of every report (the library records them on
    # the result whatever the warning filters say); printing each warning a
    # second time on stderr would only repeat them.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", GroundinsightWarning)
        try:
            return args.handler(args)
        except _UsageError as exc:
            _write(sys.stderr, f"groundinsight: error: {exc}\n")
            return EXIT_USAGE

docs.title: Statistics and classification
docs.text:
Two thin functions on top of a long-format result frame: named quantiles next to the extremes, and a class column that turns a continuous quantity into the bands a study argues in.

There is deliberately no built-in table of admissible values. Touch-voltage limits depend on the clearing time, the standard edition and the additional resistances assumed; a plausible-looking constant baked in here would be carried into a result without ever being checked. classify takes its edges from the caller, who can cite them.

docs.title: statistics
docs.text:
Summarise and classify a long-format result frame.

A parameter study produces hundreds of rows; a report needs a handful of numbers and a verdict. Polars already does the arithmetic, so these two functions add only the shape an engineering summary wants -- named quantiles next to the extremes, and a class column that turns a continuous quantity into the bands a study argues in.

Deliberately absent: any built-in table of admissible values. Touch-voltage limits depend on the clearing time, the standard edition and the additional resistances assumed, and a plausible-looking constant baked in here would be carried into a result without ever being checked. :func:classify therefore takes the edges from the caller, who can cite them.

summarize(
    frame: DataFrame,
    value: str,
    *,
    by: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    quantiles: Sequence[float] = DEFAULT_QUANTILES,
) -> pl.DataFrame

Reduce one column to count, spread, quantiles and extremes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frame DataFrame

Long-format results, e.g. from :meth:~groundinsight.simulation.sweep.SweepResult.buses.

required value str

Numeric column to summarise.

required by sequence of str

Grouping columns. Without them the whole frame is one group.

None quantiles sequence of float

Quantiles in [0, 1]. Each becomes a column p05, p50, ...

DEFAULT_QUANTILES

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

One row per group: the grouping columns, then n, n_null, n_nan, mean, std, min, the quantiles, and max. Sorted by the grouping columns so repeated runs produce identical output.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a named column is missing, if the value column is not numeric, or if a quantile lies outside [0, 1].

Notes

Read n_nan before the statistics. Polars counts a NaN as a value, not as a null: it lands in n, not in n_null, it propagates through mean, std and every quantile, and min / max skip it -- so a single NaN leaves a summary in which the extremes look sound and the mean is NaN, with nothing in the row saying why. That is a realistic input here rather than a hypothetical: a sweep point that failed under on_error="record" writes NaN into the value column. n_nan is the column that says how many, and it is 0 for an integer column, which cannot carry one.

Examples:

>>> import polars as pl
>>> from groundinsight.analysis import summarize
>>> frame = pl.DataFrame({"bus_name": ["A", "A", "B"], "EPR_V": [10.0, 30.0, 5.0]})
>>> summary = summarize(frame, "EPR_V", by=["bus_name"])
>>> summary.select("bus_name", "n", "mean", "max").rows()
[('A', 2, 20.0, 30.0), ('B', 1, 5.0, 5.0)]
Source code in src/groundinsight/analysis/statistics.py 
def summarize(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    value: str,
    *,
    by: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    quantiles: Sequence[float] = DEFAULT_QUANTILES,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Reduce one column to count, spread, quantiles and extremes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frame : pl.DataFrame
        Long-format results, e.g. from
        :meth:`~groundinsight.simulation.sweep.SweepResult.buses`.
    value : str
        Numeric column to summarise.
    by : sequence of str, optional
        Grouping columns. Without them the whole frame is one group.
    quantiles : sequence of float, optional
        Quantiles in ``[0, 1]``. Each becomes a column ``p05``, ``p50``, ...

    Returns
    -------
    pl.DataFrame
        One row per group: the grouping columns, then ``n``, ``n_null``,
        ``n_nan``, ``mean``, ``std``, ``min``, the quantiles, and ``max``.
        Sorted by the grouping columns so repeated runs produce identical
        output.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a named column is missing, if the value column is not numeric, or if
        a quantile lies outside ``[0, 1]``.

    Notes
    -----
    **Read ``n_nan`` before the statistics.** Polars counts a NaN as a
    *value*, not as a null: it lands in ``n``, not in ``n_null``, it
    propagates through ``mean``, ``std`` and every quantile, and ``min`` /
    ``max`` skip it -- so a single NaN leaves a summary in which the extremes
    look sound and the mean is NaN, with nothing in the row saying why. That
    is a realistic input here rather than a hypothetical: a sweep point that
    failed under ``on_error="record"`` writes NaN into the value column.
    ``n_nan`` is the column that says how many, and it is ``0`` for an integer
    column, which cannot carry one.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import polars as pl
    >>> from groundinsight.analysis import summarize
    >>> frame = pl.DataFrame({"bus_name": ["A", "A", "B"], "EPR_V": [10.0, 30.0, 5.0]})
    >>> summary = summarize(frame, "EPR_V", by=["bus_name"])
    >>> summary.select("bus_name", "n", "mean", "max").rows()
    [('A', 2, 20.0, 30.0), ('B', 1, 5.0, 5.0)]
    """
    missing = [c for c in [value, *(by or [])] if c not in frame.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Column(s) {missing} are not in the frame. Available: "
            f"{frame.columns}."
        )
    if not frame.schema[value].is_numeric():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Column '{value}' has dtype {frame.schema[value]}, which cannot be "
            f"summarised numerically. Cast it, or group on it with `by=` "
            f"instead of summarising it."
        )
    bad = [q for q in quantiles if not 0.0 <= q <= 1.0]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"Quantile(s) {bad} lie outside [0, 1].")

    # ``is_nan`` is only defined on the float dtypes; an integer column cannot
    # carry a NaN, so the count is a constant zero there rather than an error.
    n_nan = (
        pl.col(value).is_nan().sum().alias("n_nan")
        if frame.schema[value].is_float()
        else pl.lit(0, dtype=pl.UInt32).alias("n_nan")
    )
    aggregations = [
        pl.col(value).count().alias("n"),
        pl.col(value).null_count().alias("n_null"),
        n_nan,
        pl.col(value).mean().alias("mean"),
        pl.col(value).std().alias("std"),
        pl.col(value).min().alias("min"),
    ]
    aggregations += [
        pl.col(value).quantile(q, interpolation="linear").alias(_quantile_name(q))
        for q in quantiles
    ]
    aggregations.append(pl.col(value).max().alias("max"))

    if by:
        return frame.group_by(list(by)).agg(aggregations).sort(list(by))
    return frame.select(aggregations)

docs.text:
classify(
    frame: DataFrame,
    value: str,
    edges: Sequence[float],
    *,
    labels: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    name: str = "class",
) -> pl.DataFrame

Add a class column by binning a numeric column at the given edges.

edges are the interior boundaries: n edges make n + 1 classes. Bins are closed on the right, so a value exactly on an edge falls into the lower class -- the conservative reading when the edge is a limit.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frame DataFrame

Frame to extend.

required value str

Numeric column to classify.

required edges sequence of float

Strictly increasing interior boundaries, e.g. [80, 150] for the three bands "below 80", "80 to 150" and "above 150".

required labels sequence of str

Names for the classes, len(edges) + 1 of them. Defaults to readable interval labels built from the edges.

None name str

Name of the added column. Defaults to "class".

'class'

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

The input with one column added. Rows whose value is null or NaN get a null class rather than being forced into a band. Banded, a NaN would land in the highest class, because every NaN <= edge is false and the chain would fall through to the otherwise branch -- a failed sweep point would be reported as the worst case rather than as unassessed, and a study reading the top band as its violations would count it.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the column is missing or not numeric, if edges is empty or not strictly increasing, or if labels has the wrong length.

Examples:

>>> import polars as pl
>>> from groundinsight.analysis import classify
>>> frame = pl.DataFrame({"EPR_V": [12.0, 80.0, 450.0]})
>>> classify(frame, "EPR_V", [75.0, 300.0])["class"].to_list()
['<= 75', '75 - 300', '> 300']
Source code in src/groundinsight/analysis/statistics.py 
def classify(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    value: str,
    edges: Sequence[float],
    *,
    labels: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    name: str = "class",
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """
    Add a class column by binning a numeric column at the given edges.

    ``edges`` are the interior boundaries: ``n`` edges make ``n + 1`` classes.
    Bins are closed on the right, so a value exactly on an edge falls into the
    lower class -- the conservative reading when the edge is a limit.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frame : pl.DataFrame
        Frame to extend.
    value : str
        Numeric column to classify.
    edges : sequence of float
        Strictly increasing interior boundaries, e.g. ``[80, 150]`` for the
        three bands "below 80", "80 to 150" and "above 150".
    labels : sequence of str, optional
        Names for the classes, ``len(edges) + 1`` of them. Defaults to readable
        interval labels built from the edges.
    name : str, optional
        Name of the added column. Defaults to ``"class"``.

    Returns
    -------
    pl.DataFrame
        The input with one column added. Rows whose value is null **or NaN**
        get a null class rather than being forced into a band. Banded, a NaN
        would land in the *highest* class, because every ``NaN <= edge`` is
        false and the chain would fall through to the ``otherwise`` branch --
        a failed sweep point would be reported as the worst case rather than
        as unassessed, and a study reading the top band as its violations
        would count it.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the column is missing or not numeric, if ``edges`` is empty or not
        strictly increasing, or if ``labels`` has the wrong length.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import polars as pl
    >>> from groundinsight.analysis import classify
    >>> frame = pl.DataFrame({"EPR_V": [12.0, 80.0, 450.0]})
    >>> classify(frame, "EPR_V", [75.0, 300.0])["class"].to_list()
    ['<= 75', '75 - 300', '> 300']
    """
    if value not in frame.columns:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Column '{value}' is not in the frame. Available: {frame.columns}."
        )
    if not frame.schema[value].is_numeric():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Column '{value}' has dtype {frame.schema[value]} and cannot be "
            f"binned numerically."
        )
    edges = [float(e) for e in edges]
    if not edges:
        raise ValueError(
            "classify needs at least one edge; with none there is only one "
            "class and nothing to decide."
        )
    if any(b <= a for a, b in pairwise(edges)):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Edges must be strictly increasing, got {edges}. Overlapping or "
            f"repeated edges would make the class assignment ambiguous."
        )

    if labels is None:
        labels = [f"<= {edges[0]:g}"]
        labels += [f"{a:g} - {b:g}" for a, b in pairwise(edges)]
        labels.append(f"> {edges[-1]:g}")
    labels = list(labels)
    if len(labels) != len(edges) + 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{len(edges)} edge(s) define {len(edges) + 1} classes, but "
            f"{len(labels)} label(s) were given."
        )

    unassessable = pl.col(value).is_null()
    if frame.schema[value].is_float():
        unassessable = unassessable | pl.col(value).is_nan()
    expression = pl.when(unassessable).then(None)
    # One label per edge; the last label is the class above every edge.
    for edge, label in zip(edges, labels[:-1], strict=True):
        expression = expression.when(pl.col(value) <= edge).then(pl.lit(label))
    expression = expression.otherwise(pl.lit(labels[-1]))
    return frame.with_columns(expression.alias(name))

docs.title: Parameter sweeps
docs.text:
Solve one fault once per parameter combination and stack the results into long-format frames that carry the parameters as columns. This is what the statistics below operate on — until such a frame exists there is nothing to summarise, because every accessor on Network reports a single solve.

rho_f_points builds the points from a catalogue of five-parameter rho-f vectors, which is the form groundfield exports.

docs.title: sweep
docs.text:
Run one fault over a grid of parameter variations and collect it into one frame.

run_outage_study already answers "what changes when an element drops out". This module answers the other half: what changes when a parameter moves -- the rho-f characteristic of the faulted station, the soil resistivity, the harmonic content of the source, the fault location itself.

The unit of work is a :class:SweepPoint: a label plus the overrides that define it. Every point is applied, solved and restored, and the results are stacked into long-format Polars frames that carry the point's label and its parameters as ordinary columns. That last part is the point of the module -- until a frame like this exists there is nothing for a statistic to operate on, which is why :mod:groundinsight.analysis.statistics starts here.

Overrides are applied by writing directly onto Bus.impedance and friends, which reaches the solver untouched because run_fault does not recompute impedances (see :class:~groundinsight.electrical_network.ElectricalNetwork). Every point's overrides are undone in a finally block, and the network-level state the solves write -- stored results, active fault, path set, assembled system -- is restored exactly when the sweep ends, however it ends: a finished sweep, a failing point with on_error="raise", a cancellation through should_cancel.

Example

Vary the rho-f characteristic of the faulted station over a grid and watch what it does to the potential rise and to the parallel impedances of the two feeder directions::

points = gi.rho_f_points(
    bus="Station_7",
    k_vectors={f"k1={k1:g}": (k1, 1e-4, 3e-4, 0.0, 0.0)
               for k1 in (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1)},
    frequencies=net.frequencies,
    rho=100.0,
)
study = gi.run_sweep(
    net, fault="F_Station_7", points=points,
    cuts=[gi.Cut(name="left", branches=["C6_7"]),

)

Identifies the point in every result frame. Must be unique in a sweep.

Free-form values copied into every result row as columns, so a plot can be made against the physical parameter rather than against the label.

Build sweep points from a catalogue of rho-f parameter vectors.

Each vector is evaluated into an impedance table for bus over frequencies at the given rho, so the study varies the fitted characteristic of one station while the rest of the network stays put. k1 ... k5 and rho are copied into parameters, which puts them in the result frames as plottable columns.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default bus str

Name of the bus whose characteristic is varied.

required k_vectors dict of str to tuple

Label to (k1, k2, k3, k4, k5).

required frequencies sequence of float

Frequencies to evaluate the form at -- normally network.frequencies.

required rho float

Soil resistivity the form is evaluated at.

required

Returns:

Type Description list of SweepPoint

One point per catalogue entry, labelled with its key.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a vector produces a non-positive real part at any frequency, which the solver rejects as non-passive. The offending label and frequency are named, because an unconstrained least-squares fit can land there and the failure is otherwise reported far from its cause.

Examples:

>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> points = gi.rho_f_points(bus="bus3",
...                          k_vectors={"dry": (2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)},
...                          frequencies=[50.0], rho=100.0)
>>> [p.label for p in points], sorted(points[0].bus_impedance)

def rho_f_points(
    *,
    bus: str,
    k_vectors: Dict[str, KVector],
    frequencies: Sequence[float],
    rho: float,
) -> List[SweepPoint]:
    """
    Build sweep points from a catalogue of rho-f parameter vectors.

    Each vector is evaluated into an impedance table for ``bus`` over
    ``frequencies`` at the given ``rho``, so the study varies the *fitted
    characteristic* of one station while the rest of the network stays put.
    ``k1`` ... ``k5`` and ``rho`` are copied into ``parameters``, which puts
    them in the result frames as plottable columns.

    Parameters
    ----------
    bus : str
        Name of the bus whose characteristic is varied.
    k_vectors : dict of str to tuple
        Label to ``(k1, k2, k3, k4, k5)``.
    frequencies : sequence of float
        Frequencies to evaluate the form at -- normally ``network.frequencies``.
    rho : float
        Soil resistivity the form is evaluated at.

    Returns
    -------
    list of SweepPoint
        One point per catalogue entry, labelled with its key.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a vector produces a non-positive real part at any frequency, which
        the solver rejects as non-passive. The offending label and frequency are
        named, because an unconstrained least-squares fit can land there and the
        failure is otherwise reported far from its cause.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> points = gi.rho_f_points(bus="bus3",
    ...                          k_vectors={"dry": (2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)},
    ...                          frequencies=[50.0], rho=100.0)
    >>> [p.label for p in points], sorted(points[0].bus_impedance)
    (['dry'], ['bus3'])
    """
    points: List[SweepPoint] = []
    for label, k in k_vectors.items():
        if len(k) != 5:
            raise ValueError(
                f"rho-f vector '{label}' has {len(k)} entries; the standard "
                f"form takes exactly five, (k1, k2, k3, k4, k5)."
            )
        table: Dict[float, complex] = {}
        for freq in frequencies:
            z = _z_rho_f(tuple(k), rho, float(freq))
            if z.real <= 0.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"rho-f vector '{label}' gives Re(Z) = {z.real:.6g} Ohm at "
                    f"{freq} Hz with rho = {rho} Ohm*m, which is not a passive "
                    f"impedance and the solver will reject it. An unconstrained "
                    f"least-squares fit can produce this below the frequency "
                    f"range it was fitted on -- check the fit's validity range."
                )
            table[float(freq)] = z
        points.append(
            SweepPoint(
                label=label,
                bus_impedance={bus: table},
                parameters={
                    "bus": bus,
                    "rho_Ohm_m": rho,
                    "k1": k[0],
                    "k2": k[1],
                    "k3": k[2],
                    "k4": k[3],
                    "k5": k[4],
                },
            )
        )
    return points

def run_sweep(
    network: Network,
    *,
    fault: str,
    points: Sequence[SweepPoint],
    cuts: Optional[Sequence[Cut]] = None,
    phase_current_mode: str = "auto",
    collect_branches: bool = False,
    on_error: str = "record",
    progress: Optional[Callable[[int, int, str], None]] = None,
    should_cancel: Optional[Callable[[], bool]] = None,
) -> SweepResult:
    """
    Solve one fault once per parameter point and stack the results.

    Parameters
    ----------
    network : Network
        The network. Left exactly as found, whatever happens: the point
        overrides are undone after every point, and the stored results,
        active fault, path set and assembled system are the ones it had
        before the sweep.
    fault : str
        Fault to solve, unless a point names its own.
    points : sequence of SweepPoint
        The parameter grid. Labels must be unique.
    cuts : sequence of Cut, optional
        When given, :func:`~groundinsight.analysis.analyze_cuts` runs at every
        point and its frame is stacked into ``SweepResult.cuts()``.
    phase_current_mode : {"auto", "paths"}, optional
        Forwarded to :func:`run_fault`.
    collect_branches : bool, optional
        Branch results multiply the row count by the number of branches and are
        rarely what a parameter study plots, so they are off by default.
    on_error : {"record", "raise"}, optional
        ``"record"`` (default) notes a failing point in ``SweepResult.failures``
        and carries on -- a single non-passive parameter combination should not
        throw away the rest of a long grid. ``"raise"`` propagates instead.
    progress : callable, optional
        ``progress(done, total, label)``, called after every point (a failed
        one included) with ``total = len(points)`` and the point's label.
        See :mod:`groundinsight.progress`.
    should_cancel : callable, optional
        Asked before every point; a true answer raises
        :class:`~groundinsight.progress.StudyCancelled`.

    Returns
    -------
    SweepResult
        The stacked results of every point and the failures of the points
        that did not solve.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``points`` is empty, if two points share a label, if the fault is
        unknown, or if ``on_error`` is not one of the two accepted values.
    TypeError
        If ``progress`` or ``should_cancel`` is not callable.
    StudyCancelled
        If ``should_cancel()`` returned true; the network is as found.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import polars as pl
    >>> import groundinsight as gi
    >>> from groundinsight.api.examples import build_minimal
    >>> points = [gi.SweepPoint(label=f"Z={z}", bus_impedance={"bus3": {50.0: z}},
    ...                         parameters={"Z_bus3_Ohm": z}) for z in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0)]
    >>> study = gi.run_sweep(build_minimal(), fault="fault", points=points)
    >>> frame = study.buses().filter((pl.col("bus_name") == "bus3") & pl.col("is_rms"))
    >>> [round(v, 2) for v in frame["EPR_V"]]
    [11.73, 18.03, 24.28]
    """
    if on_error not in ("record", "raise"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"on_error must be 'record' or 'raise', got {on_error!r}."
        )
    if not points:
        raise ValueError("A sweep needs at least one point.")
    labels = [p.label for p in points]
    duplicates = {label for label in labels if labels.count(label) > 1}
    if duplicates:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Sweep point label(s) {sorted(duplicates)} appear more than once. "
            f"Labels identify the rows of every result frame and have to be "
            f"unique."
        )
    if fault not in network.faults:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Fault '{fault}' does not exist in network '{network.name}'. "
            f"Available: {sorted(network.faults)}."
        )
    hooks = StudyHooks("run_sweep", len(points), progress, should_cancel)

    bus_frames: List[pl.DataFrame] = []
    branch_frames: List[pl.DataFrame] = []
    impedance_frames: List[pl.DataFrame] = []
    cut_frames: List[pl.DataFrame] = []
    solved: List[str] = []
    failures: Dict[str, str] = {}

    # Every solve below replaces the stored result, the active fault and the
    # assembled system, and may drop the path set; restoring them exactly is
    # what "left exactly as found" means -- also for the previously active
    # fault and its cached result (S8). Bus overrides are undone per point.
    with restore_always(network):
        for point in points:
            hooks.checkpoint()
            target = point.fault or fault
            if target not in network.faults:
                message = (
                    f"point '{point.label}' names fault '{target}', which does not "
                    f"exist in network '{network.name}'"
                )
                if on_error == "raise":
                    raise ValueError(message)
                failures[point.label] = message
                hooks.advance(point.label)
                continue

            # Bound before the call, not from its return value: ``_apply`` may
            # raise after it has already mutated the network, and ``finally``
            # has to see everything it did up to that point (S2).
            saved = _new_saved()
            try:
                _apply(network, point, saved)
                if point.fault_scalings is not None:
                    fault_obj = network.faults[target]
                    saved["scalings_fault"] = target
                    saved["scalings"] = dict(fault_obj.scalings)
                    fault_obj.scalings = dict(point.fault_scalings)

                run_fault(network, target, phase_current_mode=phase_current_mode)

                bus_frames.append(_tag(network.res_buses(fault=target), point))
                if collect_branches:
                    branch_frames.append(
                        _tag(network.res_branches(fault=target), point)
                    )
                impedance_frames.append(
                    _tag(
                        network.res_all_impedances().filter(
                            pl.col("fault_name") == target
                        ),
                        point,
                    )
                )
                if cuts:
                    analysis = analyze_cuts(network, fault=target, cuts=cuts)
                    cut_frames.append(_tag(analysis.to_polars(), point))
                solved.append(point.label)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- recorded, then re-raised or not
                if on_error == "raise":
                    raise
                logger.warning(
                    "Sweep point '%s' failed and was skipped: %s", point.label, exc
                )
                failures[point.label] = str(exc)
            finally:
                _restore(network, saved)
            hooks.advance(point.label)

    result = SweepResult(fault=fault, labels=solved, failures=failures)
    result._buses = pl.concat(bus_frames, how="diagonal") if bus_frames else None
    result._branches = (
        pl.concat(branch_frames, how="diagonal") if branch_frames else None
    )
    result._impedances = (
        pl.concat(impedance_frames, how="diagonal") if impedance_frames else None
    )
    result._cuts = pl.concat(cut_frames, how="diagonal") if cut_frames else None
    if failures:
        logger.warning(
            "%d of %d sweep points failed: %s",
            len(failures),
            len(points),
            ", ".join(sorted(failures)),
        )
    return result

import groundinsight as gi is all everyday work needs: the package re-exports every public function, class and constant at the top level. This page lists each of them — the names of groundinsight.__all__ and those of the service layer groundinsight.api — with the API page that documents it, and renders the few that have no page of their own below.

import groundinsight as gi

net = gi.create_network(name="example", frequencies=[50.0])
print(len(gi.__all__) > 100, gi.__version__ == gi.show_versions()["groundinsight"])  # True True

from groundinsight import * imports exactly these names. Everything else — module internals, the ORM classes of the database, the helpers named in the internal API — can change in any release; the names below follow the deprecation policy (a renamed or removed name keeps working with a DeprecationWarning for at least two releases and six months).

groundinsight package initialisation.

Re-exports the public API surface of groundinsight: the SQLite store (Database and the module-level session helpers), the JSON project file, the top-level network factory functions (create_network, create_bus, create_branch, create_source, create_fault), the fault solver (run_fault), the outage / what-if and inverse-rho analysis helpers, the transient study workflow and the matplotlib plotting helpers. All symbols re-exported here are available as groundinsight.<name> and are listed in :data:__all__.

This module holds no implementation: imports, __all__, __version__ and the PEP 562 __getattr__ that resolves deprecated names, so importing the package binds names and nothing else. Everything else lives in a module of its own -- the logging default and :func:set_log_level in _logging, :func:show_versions in _versions, the persistence in database.store and io.project_file.

NetworkFrequencyOrderWarning(
    *args,
    code: Optional[str] = None,
    elements: Sequence[ElementRef] = (),
    severity: str = "warning",

Bases: GroundinsightWarning

Warning category for non-strictly-monotone Network.frequencies.

Emitted by :class:Network when frequencies is supplied in a non-strictly-increasing order. The FFT transient solver (:mod:groundinsight.simulation.transient) uses the order of Network.frequencies to map spectral bins to the impedance dictionary; a descending or shuffled list produces a transient with the spectral bins reversed and is almost always a user error.

Mirrors :class:groundfield.solver.engine.EngineFrequencyOrderWarning so users get consistent diagnostics across the three packages of the earthing-platform stack.

Notes

Suppress with warnings.simplefilter('ignore', NetworkFrequencyOrderWarning); surface only once per Python process by combining it with simplefilter('once', ...).

Examples:

>>> import warnings
>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
...     warnings.simplefilter("always")
...     net = gi.create_network(name="n", frequencies=[250.0, 50.0])
>>> [w.category.__name__ for w in caught]
['NetworkFrequencyOrderWarning']

def __init__(
    self,
    *args,
    code: Optional[str] = None,
    elements: Sequence[ElementRef] = (),
    severity: str = "warning",
):
    super().__init__(*args)
    if severity not in _SEVERITIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"severity must be one of {_SEVERITIES}, got {severity!r}"
        )
    self.code = code if code is not None else self.default_code
    self.elements = tuple((str(kind), str(name)) for kind, name in elements)
    self.severity = severity
    sink = _SINK.get()
    if sink is not None:
        sink.append(
            Diagnostic(
                code=self.code,
                severity=self.severity,
                category=type(self).__name__,
                message=str(self),
                elements=list(self.elements),
            )
        )

docs.text:
TransientModelWarning(
    *args,
    code: Optional[str] = None,
    elements: Sequence[ElementRef] = (),
    severity: str = "warning",
)

Bases: GroundinsightWarning

Warning category for a transient run whose model is narrower than its input.

Emitted by :mod:groundinsight.simulation.transient when the network carries something a solver path cannot represent, and the result is therefore quantitatively different from what the same network yields elsewhere. It is deliberately not an error: the remaining physics is still solved correctly and the answer is often the one the user wants, but the difference has to be visible rather than inferred from a documentation chapter.

Current cases:

  • the FFT solver meeting a branch with mutual coupling, which it does not evaluate (the stationary solver and the state-space solver do),
  • either transient solver meeting an active fault with per-frequency scalings other than 1, which is a frequency-domain concept the time-domain source waveform replaces,
  • a mutual inductance larger than the branch's own L_self, which is not physically realisable for two coupled conductors and is almost always a mH/H unit slip,
  • the state-space solver meeting a voltage source that reaches the fault, whose coupling it does not model (code TRANSIENT_COUPLING_SKIPPED), or a purely resistive branch carrying mutual data (TRANSIENT_RESISTIVE_COUPLING_IGNORED).
Notes

Suppress with warnings.simplefilter('ignore', TransientModelWarning); turn into an error with simplefilter('error', TransientModelWarning).

Examples:

>>> import groundinsight as gi
>>> issubclass(gi.TransientModelWarning, gi.GroundinsightWarning)
True

def __init__(
    self,
    *args,
    code: Optional[str] = None,
    elements: Sequence[ElementRef] = (),
    severity: str = "warning",
):
    super().__init__(*args)
    if severity not in _SEVERITIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"severity must be one of {_SEVERITIES}, got {severity!r}"
        )
    self.code = code if code is not None else self.default_code
    self.elements = tuple((str(kind), str(name)) for kind, name in elements)
    self.severity = severity
    sink = _SINK.get()
    if sink is not None:
        sink.append(
            Diagnostic(
                code=self.code,
                severity=self.severity,
                category=type(self).__name__,
                message=str(self),
                elements=list(self.elements),
            )
        )

docs.title: DCLimitWarning
docs.text:
DCLimitWarning(
    *args,
    code: Optional[str] = None,
    elements: Sequence[ElementRef] = (),
    severity: str = "warning",
)

Bases: GroundinsightWarning

Something about a formula at 0 Hz needed a decision rather than a value.

Raised in four situations, all of them at f = 0 only:

  • the imaginary part at DC is dropped and is not small enough to be numerical dust -- a reactance cannot survive at DC, so the value is a modelling statement that the real-part fallback silently overrides;
  • the limit is not well resolved, i.e. the last decade of the approach sequence still moved the real part appreciably and the step did not shrink at least five-fold from the decade before -- how sqrt(f) or log(f) behave near DC;
  • the approach sequence diverges and the element is treated as an open circuit;
  • an impedance is zero (or too small to invert) at DC and is replaced by the small finite substitute of :func:dc_substitute_impedance.

It is a warning and not an error on purpose: in every one of the four cases there is a defensible value to continue with, and a DC study that stops on the first unusual formula is of no use. Promote it with warnings.simplefilter("error", DCLimitWarning) to make a study strict.

A real part of minus infinity -- log(f) at 0 Hz -- is deliberately not a fifth case: it is the limit of a negative resistance, there is no defensible value to continue with, and :func:check_passive_impedance refuses it like any negative real part.

>>> issubclass(gi.DCLimitWarning, gi.GroundinsightWarning)

set_log_level(
