docs.title: Result tables
docs.text:
Every solve stores one Result per fault on the network, and the package hands results out as Polars data frames: the res_* accessors of Network, the study results, the thermal checks and the importers. This page lists every column of every frame with its type, unit and meaning.

The column names and types in the tables below are generated from the code when this site is built — from the schema constants that pin the frames (RES_BUSES_SCHEMA, gi.RES_FAULT_SCHEMA, CUT_FRAME_SCHEMA, …) or, where a frame has no constant, from a frame built on a small network at build time. A test compares the constants with the frames of a real solve, so a table cannot describe a column the code no longer has.

docs.title: Rules that hold for every frame
docs.text:
Units. Phasors are RMS values, currents in A, voltages in V, impedances in Ω, angles in degrees; the column name ends with the unit (_A, _V, _Ohm, _degree or _deg, _Hz, _s, _mm2). The time series of a transient study are instantaneous values. See Conventions and units.

Signs. Magnitudes do not depend on a sign convention, angles do. Earth potentials, electrode currents and injections are reported in the earth-side frame (a current that enters the earthing network at the source and leaves it at the fault), branch currents for the physical fault, counted from from_bus to to_bus — see Signs and phase angles.

Frequencies and the RMS row. frequency_Hz is Float64 in every frame of a solve. res_buses, res_branches and res_fault add one RMS row per element that combines all frequencies as \(\sqrt{\sum_f |X(f)|^2}\); that row has is_rms true and frequency_Hz null, and its angles, ratios and impedances are null, because they have no RMS. res_all_impedances and the decomposition frame have no RMS row. The exception are the comparison frames of an outage study: there frequency_Hz is text — "50.0", or "RMS" for the RMS row — because it is the key the scenarios are joined on. Filter with pl.col("is_rms") in the frames of a solve and with pl.col("frequency_Hz") == "RMS" in a comparison frame.

Two reduction factors. reduction_factor (in res_fault: r_epr) is the EPR ratio with and without the inductive coupling — a property of the line, blind to the electrodes, and not the reduction factor of EN 50522. reduction_factor_current (in res_fault: r_current) is |I_E| / |I_F|, the reduction factor r of EN 50522. They coincide only for ideally bonded stations; see Which reduction factor is which.

Missing values. A quantity the result marks as undefined is null, never a number: the current-based factor at a frequency without fault current, the earthing impedance of a fault bus without an electrode in its earthing group (diagnostic EARTHING_IMPEDANCE_UNDEFINED, see Warnings and diagnostics). The schemas are pinned, so an empty result is an empty frame with these columns, which can still be selected and filtered.

import polars as pl
import groundinsight as gi

station = gi.BusType(name="station", system_type="Station", voltage_level=20.0,
                     impedance_formula="2.0")
cable = gi.BranchType(name="cable", grounding_conductor=True,
                      self_impedance_formula="(0.2 + j*2*pi*f*1.2e-3)*l",
                      mutual_impedance_formula="(j*2*pi*f*1.0e-3)*l")
net = gi.create_network(name="tables", frequencies=[50.0, 250.0])
for name in ("UW", "S1", "S2"):
    gi.create_bus(name=name, type=station, network=net)
gi.create_branch(name="K1", type=cable, from_bus="UW", to_bus="S1", length=1.0, network=net)
gi.create_branch(name="K2", type=cable, from_bus="S1", to_bus="S2", length=1.0, network=net)
gi.create_source(name="infeed", bus="UW", values={50.0: 1000.0, 250.0: 50.0}, network=net)
gi.create_fault(name="F", bus="S2", network=net)
gi.run_fault(net, "F")

buses = net.res_buses(fault="F")
at_50_hz = buses.filter(pl.col("frequency_Hz") == 50.0)    # one row per bus
rms = buses.filter(pl.col("is_rms"))                       # one row per bus, frequency_Hz null
print(buses.shape, at_50_hz.shape, rms["frequency_Hz"].null_count())   # (9, 10) (3, 10) 3

study = gi.run_outage_study(net, fault="F", scenarios=[gi.Outage(name="K2 out", disabled_branches=["K2"])])
compared = study.compare_buses()
print(compared.schema["frequency_Hz"])                     # String
print(compared.filter(pl.col("frequency_Hz") == "RMS").height)   # 6: 3 buses x 2 scenarios

docs.title: Network.res_buses(fault=None)
docs.text:
One row per bus and frequency plus one RMS row per bus, for one fault or for every stored result. I_bus_A is the current through the bus's own electrode into the soil; I_inj_A is the current of the earthing conductor at a source or fault bus. Sizing an earthing conductor with I_bus_A underestimates it — the thermal check of the node uses the right one for each element.

Column Type Unit Meaning bus_name String – name of the bus fault String – name of the fault the result belongs to frequency_Hz Float64 Hz frequency of the row; null on the RMS row is_rms Boolean – true on the one RMS row per element, which combines all frequencies as √Σ|X(f)|² EPR_V Float64 V earth potential rise of the bus, ResultBus.uepr_freq; RMS row: ResultBus.uepr EPR_degree Float64 ° angle of the EPR in the earth-side sign frame (see Conventions); null on the RMS row I_bus_A Float64 A electrode current: what the bus's own electrode passes into the soil, ResultBus.ia_freq; summed over all buses it is zero I_bus_degree Float64 ° angle of I_bus_A; null on the RMS row I_inj_A Float64 A current of the earthing conductor at a source or fault bus, ResultBus.i_inj_freq -- the source current at a source bus, the fault current at the fault bus, 0 elsewhere; the quantity a conductor is sized for I_inj_degree Float64 ° angle of I_inj_A; null on the RMS row

docs.title: Network.res_branches(fault=None)
docs.text:
One row per branch and frequency plus one RMS row per branch.

Column Type Unit Meaning branch_name String – name of the branch fault String – name of the fault the result belongs to frequency_Hz Float64 Hz frequency of the row; null on the RMS row is_rms Boolean – true on the one RMS row per element, which combines all frequencies as √Σ|X(f)|² I_branch_A Float64 A current of the earthing conductor (cable screen, earth wire) of the branch, ResultBranch.i_s_freq; counted positive from from_bus to to_bus for the physical fault I_branch_degree Float64 ° angle of I_branch_A; null on the RMS row

docs.title: Network.res_all_impedances()
docs.text:
One row per stored fault and frequency, no RMS row: the earthing impedance and both reduction factors at the fault location.

Column Type Unit Meaning fault_name String – name of the fault (this frame says fault_name, the others fault) fault_bus String – bus the fault sits on frequency_Hz Float64 Hz frequency of the row; the frame has no RMS row grounding_impedance_Ohm Float64 Ω earthing impedance Z_E of EN 50522 at the fault bus: the driving-point impedance of the earthing network seen from there (ResultGroundingImpedance.value, equal to z_earthing); null where it is undefined grounding_impedance_deg Float64 ° angle of Z_E reduction_factor Float64 – value: EPR at the fault bus with the inductive coupling over the EPR without it -- a property of the line, not the r of EN 50522 reduction_factor_current Float64 – value_current: |I_E| / |I_F|, the reduction factor r of EN 50522

docs.title: Network.res_fault(fault)
docs.text:
The key figures of one fault, read from the stored result: one row per network frequency plus one RMS row. The schema is gi.RES_FAULT_SCHEMA; this is the frame the EN 50522 how-to and the command line report.

Column Type Unit Meaning fault String – name of the fault fault_bus String – bus the result was computed for frequency_Hz Float64 Hz frequency of the row; null on the RMS row is_rms Boolean – true on the one RMS row per element, which combines all frequencies as √Σ|X(f)|² I_F_A Float64 A fault current I_F (3I_0 of EN 50522): the currents of the sources that reach the fault, times the fault scalings (ResultReductionFactor.i_fault); RMS row √Σ|I_F(f)|² I_F_degree Float64 ° angle of I_F; null on the RMS row EPR_fault_V Float64 V earth potential rise of the fault bus; RMS row: its stored RMS value EPR_fault_degree Float64 ° angle of that EPR; null on the RMS row EPR_max_V Float64 V largest earth potential rise of any bus at that frequency (RMS row: largest RMS value) EPR_max_bus String – the bus where EPR_max_V occurs r_epr Float64 – EPR-based reduction factor value -- not the r of EN 50522; null on the RMS row r_current Float64 – current-based reduction factor value_current = |I_E| / |I_F|, the r of EN 50522; null on the RMS row and where it is undefined I_E_A Float64 A earth-return current I_E (i_earth); RMS row √Σ|I_E(f)|² U_E_V Float64 V earthing voltage U_E of EN 50522: the EPR at the fault bus (u_earthing); RMS row √Σ|U_E(f)|², the value compared with U_Tp Z_E_Ohm Float64 Ω earthing impedance Z_E of EN 50522, the driving point of the earthing network at the fault bus (z_earthing); null on the RMS row Z_E_degree Float64 ° angle of Z_E; null on the RMS row n_diagnostics Int64 – number of records in Result.diagnostics, the same on every row

docs.title: SweepResult.buses(), .branches(), .impedances(), .cuts()
docs.text: A parameter sweep stacks the frames of its points: buses() the rows of res_buses, branches() those of res_branches (collected only with run_sweep(..., collect_branches=True)), impedances() those of res_all_impedances for the swept fault, and cuts() those of CutAnalysis.to_polars() (only with cuts=). Each frame starts with the column point (String, the SweepPoint.label) followed by one column per key of SweepPoint.parameters — rho_f_points adds bus, rho_Ohm_m and k1 … k5 — and then the columns of the frame it stacks, with the types listed above. A frame with nothing collected is an empty frame without columns. See Parameter sweeps and statistics.

docs.title: OutageStudyResult.compare_buses() and .compare_branches()
docs.text:
Long format, one row per element, frequency, scenario and metric, with the difference to a reference scenario (against=, by default the base case). frequency_Hz is text here (see above).

Column Type Unit Meaning bus_name String – name of the bus frequency_Hz String – frequency as text ("50.0") or "RMS" -- the join key of the comparison, not a number metric String – the compared res_buses column, EPR_V unless columns= names others value Float64 unit of the metric the metric in this scenario scenario String – scenario label (base for the unmodified network) delta_vs_base Float64 unit of the metric value minus the reference scenario's value; the suffix is the reference label (against=) delta_pct_vs_base Float64 % 100 · delta / reference value; null where the reference value is 0 Column Type Unit Meaning branch_name String – name of the branch frequency_Hz String – frequency as text ("50.0") or "RMS" metric String – the compared res_branches column, I_branch_A unless columns= names others value Float64 unit of the metric the metric in this scenario scenario String – scenario label delta_vs_base Float64 unit of the metric value minus the reference scenario's value delta_pct_vs_base Float64 % 100 · delta / reference value; null where the reference value is 0

docs.title: CutAnalysis.to_polars()

One row per direction (cut) and frequency of gi.analyze_cuts.

Column Type Unit Meaning fault String – the analysed fault fault_bus String – bus the fault sits on, the reference point of the decomposition cut String – name of the direction (a Cut, or the implicit rest / source_loop side) side_buses String – buses seen through that cut, comma-separated n_side_buses Int64 – number of buses on that side branches String – branches of the cut, comma-separated sides_are_disjoint Boolean – true when no two directions reach the same bus; the far-side currents are defined only then frequency_Hz Float64 Hz frequency of the row (no RMS row) Z_side_Ohm Float64 Ω parallel impedance of that direction, from source-free current division Z_side_deg Float64 ° its angle Z_local_Ohm Float64 Ω impedance of the fault bus's own electrode Z_parallel_Ohm Float64 Ω Z_local in parallel with every Z_side Z_driving_point_Ohm Float64 Ω driving-point impedance of the solved nodal system at the fault bus identity_residual Float64 – |Z_parallel − Z_driving_point| / |Z_driving_point|; grows when the decomposition misses a current path I_fault_A Float64 A injection at the fault bus I_local_A Float64 A part of it taken by the fault bus's own electrode I_shield_A Float64 A shield current leaving the fault bus in that direction I_shield_deg Float64 ° its angle current_share Float64 – |I_shield| / |I_fault| I_earth_A Float64 A soil current crossing the cut, summed over the far side; null when the directions overlap I_total_A Float64 A total current crossing the cut; null when the directions overlap r_side Float64 – |I_earth| / |I_total|, the earth-return share of that direction kcl_residual Float64 – |I_fault − I_local − Σ I_shield| / |I_fault|; zero confirms the split accounts for the whole fault current

docs.title: summarize(frame, value, by=...) and classify(frame, value, edges)
docs.text: summarize returns one row per group: the grouping columns, then n, n_null, n_nan, mean, std, min, one column per quantile (p05, p50, p95 by default) and max — read n_nan first, a NaN propagates into the mean and the quantiles. classify returns its input with one String column added (class unless name= says otherwise); a null or NaN value gets a null class.

docs.title: Warnings and diagnostics
docs.text: groundinsight reports a condition that changes how a result must be read — a heuristic phase-current split, a frequency the input does not cover, a reactance that has no meaning at 0 Hz — as a warning with a stable code, not as a log line. This page lists every code the package can produce: the warning class it is raised with, its severity, the elements it names, when it is raised and what to do about it. A test compares the page with the source code in both directions, so a code cannot be added without a row here.

docs.title: How a diagnostic reaches you
docs.text:
Every package warning is an instance of a subclass of gi.GroundinsightWarning (itself a UserWarning) and carries three fields next to its message:

Field Meaning code stable upper-case identifier; programs branch on it, never on the message text severity info, warning or error (only the pre-flight check produces error) elements the network elements concerned, as (kind, name) pairs, e.g. ("branch", "K2"); kinds are bus, branch, source, fault, bus_type, branch_type, network and switch (a pandapower switch, by its import label)

Where you find them:

  • During a solve. gi.run_fault and gi.solve collect every package warning of the run into Result.diagnostics, a list of gi.Diagnostic records with code, severity, category, message and elements. The record is made even when the warning is filtered out or shown only once, so the result always carries its full set; Network.res_fault counts them in n_diagnostics.
  • Around any other call (importing, creating elements, a thermal check, a transient study), collect them yourself with groundinsight.diagnostics.collecting(): with collecting() as records: .... The collection is per thread and per asyncio task, so two runs in parallel never see each other's records.
  • Before a solve. gi.check_network(net) returns the problems of a network as gi.Diagnostic records without raising; its codes are listed below.
  • In a front end. The service layer groundinsight.api passes the records on unchanged as DiagnosticDTO (code, severity, category, elements, message).

A worked example of all four: Diagnostics, logging and warnings.

As Python warnings they also follow the usual machinery: warnings.simplefilter("error", gi.ModelAssumptionWarning) turns a category into an exception (useful in CI), python -W error::groundinsight.DCLimitWarning does the same from the command line, and logging.captureWarnings(True) routes them into logging. Renamed parameters and deprecated attributes raise Python's own DeprecationWarning, which has no code.

docs.title: Warning classes
docs.text: Code Category Severity Elements Raised when What to do GROUNDINSIGHT GroundinsightWarning warning – Default code of the base class (a UserWarning); every package warning is an instance of it. The package raises its subclasses with their own codes. Filter or catch gi.GroundinsightWarning to handle all package warnings at once. MODEL_ASSUMPTION ModelAssumptionWarning warning – Default code of the class for results that rest on a modelling assumption or heuristic; the package raises it with the specific codes below. Read the specific code. INPUT InputWarning warning – Default code of the class for input that is incomplete or inconsistent but can be solved; the package raises it with the specific codes below. Read the specific code. FREQUENCY_ORDER NetworkFrequencyOrderWarning warning – Network.frequencies is not strictly increasing. The order is kept, but the FFT transient solver maps spectral bins by position. Sort the list, unless the order is intended. DC_LIMIT DCLimitWarning warning – An impedance formula is evaluated at 0 Hz and the limit needs a decision: it has a pole (modelled as an open circuit — right for a series capacitance), it converges only slowly (the value reached is an approximation of the limit, e.g. sqrt(f) or log(f) terms), it carries a finite reactance (the 0 Hz bin takes the real part and drops the reactance), or it is zero (an ideal short: modelled with a stand-in of √ε times the smallest other impedance of the network). Only the 0 Hz bin is affected. Write reactances as j*2*pi*f*L so they vanish at DC; state a known DC value as a term without f; give an ideal bond a small resistance or merge its two buses. See Formula syntax: direct current. TRANSIENT_MODEL TransientModelWarning warning coupled branches (FFT coupling case) The transient model is narrower than the input: the FFT solver ignores mutual coupling (the EPR comes out higher, i.e. conservative), the FFT window ends while the response still rings (the tail wraps around), the active fault carries scalings other than 1 (both solvers use the waveform as the literal injection), or a branch has |M_mutual| > L_self (almost always a unit slip). Use solver="state_space" for coupled networks; lengthen t_end or pass zero_pad=True; scale the waveform itself; check the units of the RLC formulas.

docs.title: Codes raised during a solve
docs.text:
These are raised by gi.run_fault and gi.solve and stored in Result.diagnostics.

Code Category Severity Elements Raised when What to do PHASE_PROXY ModelAssumptionWarning warning the branches of the mesh, the fault The phase network is meshed (a ring, parallel cables) and branches of the mesh have no phase_impedance_formula, so the phase current is split with proxy impedances (the screen self impedance, or the length). Broken screens are named. Declare phase_impedance_formula on the branch types — the reduced phase impedance, see Phase impedance for rings and meshes. THEVENIN_COUPLING ModelAssumptionWarning warning the voltage sources A Thévenin (voltage) source away from the fault bus reaches the fault while a coupled branch has a mutual impedance. The coupling is driven by the source's Norton current instead of its loop current; in the reference cases the EPR came out 6–38 % too low, i.e. unconservative. Model the infeed as a current source with the fault current of a short-circuit calculation, or treat the EPR as a lower bound. SCALINGS_INCOMPLETE InputWarning warning the fault Fault.scalings is a non-empty mapping that misses network frequencies; those are scaled with 1.0 (full contribution). Once per run. Also reported by gi.check_network. Give every network frequency a scaling; 0.0 excludes a frequency. Leaving scalings out means 1.0 everywhere, without a warning. SOURCE_FREQUENCY_GAP InputWarning warning the source A source that reaches the fault has no value at some network frequencies and contributes 0 A there. Once per source and run. Also reported by gi.check_network. Complete Source.values, or accept the gap deliberately. A source with a value at no network frequency is an error (ValueError). SOURCE_WITHOUT_PHASE_PATH ModelAssumptionWarning warning the source, the fault A source reaches the fault through the earthing network but has no phase-conductor connection to the fault bus. Its current is still injected, as if it returned entirely through soil and screens (reduction factor 1 for its share, no coupling). Check the topology and the active flags; a phase path needs branches that carry a phase conductor. EARTH_GROUP_UNDEFINED ModelAssumptionWarning warning the fault, the fault bus No electrode carries more than numerical noise (1e-9 of the fault current), so there is no earth-return current: i_earth and value_current are None. Usually a fault on the bus of the only source, or a network without electrodes; check the excitation. FAULT_AT_FEEDING_BUS ModelAssumptionWarning info the fault, the fault bus The fault sits on the bus of every source that feeds it: the fault current closes through that station's own earthing back to the source, nothing is injected into the earthing network, EPR and earth-return current are zero, and both reduction factors are None. U_E is 0 V; Z_E is still the driving-point impedance. Recorded in Result.diagnostics only (groundinsight.diagnostics.note), never raised as a Python warning. Nothing to fix for the station itself; to study what the surrounding network sees, place the fault at another bus or add the other infeeds. EARTH_GROUP_SPREAD ModelAssumptionWarning warning the fault, the fault bus The electrode currents are spread in angle, so the split into the group that feeds the soil and the group that returns the current is less sharp than usual; I_E and value_current describe the dominant direction. Read r_current with care; compare with the EPR itself. REDUCTION_FACTOR_UNDEFINED ModelAssumptionWarning warning the fault, the fault bus The EPR of the fault bus without coupling is zero to numerical precision (or the solve without coupling fails), so the EPR-based factor value has no reference and is None at that frequency. Expected for a fault without a path to earth at that frequency; the EN 50522 factor value_current is unaffected. EARTHING_IMPEDANCE_UNDEFINED ModelAssumptionWarning warning the fault, the fault bus, the buses of its earthing group No bus connected to the fault bus through screens has an electrode, or the fault bus reaches the earthing network only through a Thévenin loop: z_earthing and Z_G are None. Give the earthing group an electrode; a Thévenin loop is not an earthing impedance. PARALLEL_COEFFICIENT_DEFAULT ModelAssumptionWarning warning the sources Legacy mode phase_current_mode="paths": a source reaches the fault over several paths whose parallel_coefficient is left at the default, so each path carries the full current. Use the default mode "auto", or set the coefficients.

DC_LIMIT and FREQUENCY_ORDER can appear in Result.diagnostics as well, when an impedance is evaluated during the run; see Warning classes.

docs.title: Codes raised outside a solve
docs.text:
These are raised by the function named in the row; collect them with collecting() around the call.

Code Category Severity Elements Raised when What to do SOURCE_FREQUENCY_OUTSIDE_NETWORK InputWarning warning the source create_source, create_voltage_source or Network.add_source get values at frequencies the network does not solve; they are ignored. Also reported by gi.check_network. Add the frequency to Network.frequencies, or drop the value. THERMAL_DATA_INCOMPLETE InputWarning warning the branches or buses, the fault check_conductor_limits / check_node_limits: a type declares half of its thermal data (a material without a cross-section, or the reverse), so within_limit is null for it. Declare both, or neither. THERMAL_DC_EXCLUDED ModelAssumptionWarning warning the branches or buses, the fault The 0 Hz component is left out of the adiabatic check, because m already carries the DC content of an alternating fault current. A genuine direct current during T_k adds about I_dc² to I_th²; the message quotes the increase. If a direct current really flows during the fault (DC railway, rectifier), check with the increased I_th. SC_KAPPA_MIXED ModelAssumptionWarning warning the sources, the fault resolve_fault_sc_characteristics: the sources feeding the fault have different R/X; the non-linear IEC 60909 factors are applied once, with the aggregated κ. Use the transient solver for an exact result with mixed R/X. SC_DATA_INCOMPLETE InputWarning warning the sources, the fault resolve_fault_sc_characteristics: sources that carry part of the current have no IEC 60909 data; κ is that of the others. Set i_k_a, r_to_x or kappa on every source. SC_KAPPA_MISSING InputWarning warning the buses read_shortcircuit_results: neither ip_ka nor a usable R/X is available for a bus. Complete the zero-sequence data in pandapower (x0x_max, r0x0_max, r0_ohm_per_km, …). SC_KAPPA_OUT_OF_RANGE InputWarning warning the bus read_shortcircuit_results: pandapower's ip_ka/ikss_ka imply a κ outside (1, 2]. Check the pandapower case. SC_ROW_AMBIGUOUS InputWarning warning the fault, the bus apply_shortcircuit_characteristics: several rows match the fault bus; the first is used. Pass pp_bus= or bus_name=. SC_SPLIT_EQUAL InputWarning warning the sources, the fault apply_shortcircuit_characteristics: the sources inject nothing at the frequency, so I_k'' is split equally. Set the relative infeed shares first. SC_VALUE_REPLACED InputWarning warning the fault apply_shortcircuit_characteristics replaced a different t_k_s or n_factor of the fault with the value of the short-circuit case. Pass the value explicitly if the previous one was intended. SC_VOLTAGE_SOURCE_SKIPPED InputWarning warning the source apply_shortcircuit_characteristics: a voltage source keeps its values. Model the infeed as a current source if its share should be written. IMPORT_BUS_SKIPPED InputWarning warning the bus from_pandapower / preview_pandapower_import: a bus has no usable vn_kv. Fix vn_kv in pandapower. IMPORT_LINE_SKIPPED InputWarning warning the branch A line is a self-loop, or its length cannot be imported. Fix the line in pandapower. IMPORT_LENGTH_DEFAULT InputWarning warning the branch A line has no usable length_km and gets the fallback of 1 km. Set length_km; every impedance of the branch scales with it. IMPORT_SWITCH_NOT_IMPORTED InputWarning warning the buses the switches would bond Closed bus-to-bus switches were not imported because ImportDefaults.switch_branch_type is not set; a bus behind such a switch is isolated and reads 0 V. Set switch_branch_type. IMPORT_LINE_SWITCH_OPEN InputWarning info the branch, the switches from_pandapower: a line has an open line switch (et="l") and is imported with an open phase conductor (phase_impedance_formula = "nan"); it carries no fault current, its screen stays connected at both ends. Nothing, if the screen is bonded at both stations; set the branch inactive if it is interrupted as well. IMPORT_ELEMENT_NOT_IMPORTED InputWarning warning – Transformers and impedance elements are not modelled and were left out. Check the preview; model the connection by hand if it matters. IMPORT_VOLTAGE_LEVEL_MISMATCH InputWarning warning the bus type The default bus type declares another voltage level than voltage_level_kV. Use a bus type written for the imported level. IMPORT_EMPTY InputWarning warning the network The import produced no bus or no branch — usually a wrong voltage_level_kV. Check voltage_level_kV against net.bus.vn_kv. TRANSIENT_SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED InputWarning warning the sources TransientStudy.solve(solver="fft"): a source with a waveform has no galvanic connection to the fault bus and injects nothing. Check the topology. TRANSIENT_BRANCH_SKIPPED InputWarning warning the branches State-space solver: branches without R_self/L_self are left out. Declare R_self_formula and L_self_formula on the branch types. TRANSIENT_COUPLING_SKIPPED TransientModelWarning warning the voltage sources State-space solver: the coupling is modelled for current sources only. Use current sources for coupled studies. TRANSIENT_RESISTIVE_COUPLING_IGNORED TransientModelWarning warning the branches State-space solver: R_mutual/M_mutual on branches without L_self are ignored. Give those branches an inductance. TRANSIENT_PHASE_SPLIT ModelAssumptionWarning warning the coupled branches State-space solver on a meshed network: the phase split is taken at f_eval and depends on frequency here, so a DC offset and harmonics are split as at f_eval (below 1 % of the peak on a mixed cable/line ring). Accept, or compare with run_fault at the frequencies of interest. PROJECT_FILE_LEGACY_ENCODING InputWarning warning the network load_network_from_json read a file that is not UTF-8 (written by 0.6.0 or earlier on a non-UTF-8 system) with the platform encoding. Save it again; the new file is UTF-8. LEGACY_EARTHING_DEFINITION InputWarning info the fault A result stored before U_E and Z_E were redefined at the fault bus is loaded: its old values moved to u_earthing_group / z_earthing_group, and U_E, Z_E and Z_G stay empty. A record in Result.diagnostics, not a Python warning. Run the fault again.

docs.title: Codes of the pre-flight check
docs.text:
gi.check_network(net, fault=None) returns these as records of category InputWarning (the three codes it shares with the solve — SCALINGS_INCOMPLETE, SOURCE_FREQUENCY_GAP, SOURCE_FREQUENCY_OUTSIDE_NETWORK — are listed above). An error means that run_fault would raise or would return an answer that does not describe the network; a warning that the network solves but part of the input has no effect.

Code Category Severity Elements Raised when What to do NOT_A_NETWORK InputWarning error – The argument is not a Network. Pass a network. CHECK_FAILED InputWarning error the network A check raised on an unforeseen malformation; the other checks still ran. Read the message; it names the check. ELEMENT_INVALID InputWarning error the entry An entry of buses, branches, sources or faults is not an element of the expected type. Rebuild the entry through the API. FREQUENCIES_INVALID InputWarning error the network Empty frequency list, duplicates, non-finite or negative values (an in-place edit bypasses the validator). Assign a valid list to Network.frequencies. NO_ACTIVE_BUS InputWarning error the network No bus is active. Activate the buses. NO_SOURCE InputWarning error the network The network has no source. Add a source. NO_FAULT InputWarning error the network The network has no fault. Add a fault. FAULT_UNKNOWN InputWarning error the fault The fault= argument names no fault of the network. Check the name. BRANCH_UNKNOWN_BUS InputWarning error the branch A branch end names a bus that does not exist; the solver would drop the branch. Fix the reference. SOURCE_UNKNOWN_BUS InputWarning error the source A source names a bus that does not exist; the solver would ignore it. Fix the reference. FAULT_UNKNOWN_BUS InputWarning error the fault A fault names a bus that does not exist. Fix the reference. FAULT_BUS_INACTIVE InputWarning error the fault, the bus A fault sits on an inactive bus. Activate the bus or move the fault. SOURCE_BUS_INACTIVE InputWarning warning the source, the bus A source sits on an inactive bus and injects nothing. Activate the bus if the source should feed. IMPEDANCE_MISSING InputWarning error the element An element of the nodal system has no impedance at a network frequency. Re-derive it (assign the type again) or complete the dictionary. FORMULA_ERROR InputWarning error the element No stored impedance, and the type formula cannot be evaluated. Fix the formula; see Formula syntax. IMPEDANCE_NOT_PASSIVE InputWarning error the element An impedance that is inverted is zero, too small to invert or has a negative real part. Check the formula at the lowest ρ, frequency and length of the model. IMPEDANCE_NOT_FINITE InputWarning error the element An impedance is NaN at a network frequency. Fix the formula or the stored value. SOURCE_FREQUENCY_NONE InputWarning error the source A source has a value at none of the network frequencies (run_fault raises a ValueError). Give it values at the network frequencies. SOURCE_VALUE_NOT_FINITE InputWarning error the source A source value is NaN or infinite at a network frequency. Fix the value. FAULT_NOT_REACHED InputWarning warning the fault No source reaches the fault over active elements; every potential is 0 V. Correct for an outage that islands the fault bus; otherwise check the topology. ISOLATED_BUS InputWarning warning the bus An active bus has no active branch to another active bus. Connect it or deactivate it. FLOATING_ISLAND InputWarning error the buses of the island Buses joined by grounding conductors have no electrode and therefore no reference to earth; their potential is undefined and run_fault refuses the network. Give one bus of the group an electrode.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Conditions that leave no meaningful answer raise instead of warning:

  • ValueError — invalid input or a violated model rule: an unknown element name, a formula the guard refuses, a non-passive impedance, a source without a value at any network frequency, a group of buses without a path to earth ("Singular admittance matrix … no path to reference earth"), a project file with a newer schema_version than the running release supports.
  • RuntimeError — a state that does not allow the call: no started database session for the module-level helpers, a database written by an older release opened with migrate=False, res_fault for a fault without stored result. gi.StudyCancelled, raised when a study's should_cancel() answers true, is a RuntimeError too.
  • TypeError — a value of the wrong type for a model field, or a callback that is not callable.
  • ImportError — a function of the optional pandapower extra without pandapower installed; the message names the extra.
